item.title: Employers, contractors and employees should be aware of electrical safety at work during rainstorms
item.description:
As the rainstorm warning has been issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, the Labour Department (LD) reminds employers and contractors that they should adopt necessary work arrangements and take suitable safety measures to protect the safety of their employees when they are carrying out electrical work or handling electrical plant.

     A spokesman for the LD said today (October 4) that employers and contractors should avoid assigning employees to carry out electrical work (such as electric arc welding work) or handle electrical plant at places affected by rainstorms, and should refer to the "Code of Practice in Times of Adverse Weather and 'Extreme Conditions'" and the "Guide on Safety at Work in times of Inclement Weather" issued by the LD.

     Even if electrical work is carried out or electrical plant is handled at places not affected by a rainstorm, suitable safety measures must still be adopted to prevent an electric shock as the air would be more humid. Such measures include:

(i) Ensure that all live parts of an electrical installation are isolated from the power supply source and rendered dead, and the isolation from the power supply source must be maintained as long as electrical work is being carried out;

(ii) Before carrying out any electrical work or handling any electrical plant, cut off and lock out the power supply source, then test the circuit concerned to confirm that it is dead and display suitable warning notices, and issue a work permit thereafter;

(iii) Ensure that protective devices (such as suitable and adequate fuses and circuit breakers) for the electrical installations or electrical plant have been installed and maintained in good working order, and portable electric tools must be double-insulated or properly earthed;

(iv) Provide suitable personal protective equipment such as insulating gloves and insulating mats for employees; and

(v) If live electrical work is unavoidable, a comprehensive risk assessment should be conducted by a competent person and the appropriate safety precautions should be taken to remove or properly control the electrical hazards involved before such work can proceed.

     In addition, employees should co-operate with the employer or contractor to follow the safety instructions and use the safety equipment provided.

     The LD has published guidebooks and leaflets on electrical work safety. These safety publications are available free from divisional offices of the department or can be downloaded from its website (www.labour.gov.hk/eng/public/content2_8.htm).

     Should there be any questions about occupational safety and health matters, please contact the Occupational Safety Officer of the LD at 2559 2297.

item.title: North East New Territories Landfill Extension fully opens today
item.description:
The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) announced today (October 4) that the North East New Territories (NENT) Landfill Extension has commenced full operation today, taking over from the original NENT Landfill as one of the major terminal waste management facilities in the territory. The original landfill will cease operation later this year and undergo restoration.

     The NENT Landfill Extension is located to the southeast of the original landfill and has a design landfill capacity of about 19 million cubic metres. The essential works of the landfill extension, including site formation, installation of impermeable liners, construction of a surface water collection system, as well as provision of leachate treatment and landfill gas management systems, have been completed in the middle of this year. Trial operation involving limited waste reception has subsequently commenced, along with the phased transition of landfilling operation to the landfill extension.

     The EPD will remain committed to enhancing the operation and management standards of the landfill extension, as well as its environmental and safety performance. Meanwhile, the EPD will take forward the remaining restoration and greening works at the original landfill at full speed.

item.title: Security Bureau holds Huanggang Port community experience day (with photos/video)
item.description:
In anticipation of the upcoming opening of the redeveloped Huanggang Port, the Security Bureau today (October 4) organised a community experience day, inviting members of the public from all districts to visit and tour the Huanggang Port Building Hong Kong Port Area. Participants used the public transport services connecting to the port and facilities inside the port building, and learned about the novel "collaborative inspection and joint clearance" mode as well as the building's architectural design features.

     Through the co-ordination of the Home Affairs Department with the District Offices across all 18 districts, more than 1 500 members of the public from various districts participated in the event. Participants travelled from designated pick-up points in their districts to the Huanggang Port Hong Kong Port Area by franchised buses or cross-boundary coach services. They toured the port building in groups guided by officers from the Fire Services Department and the Correctional Services Department.

     Participants first arrived at and visited the public transport interchange of the port building to learn about the public transport arrangements. They then toured the port building to learn about its interior design features and experience various passenger-friendly facilities, including the free Government Wi-Fi service. They subsequently took the escalators to the departure hall on the fifth floor, where officers of the Immigration Department introduced the operation of the "collaborative inspection" automated channels, giving participants a better understanding of the novel "collaborative inspection and joint clearance" mode. Officers of Hong Kong Customs then explained the passenger clearance and customs inspection procedures at the arrival hall on the fourth floor.

     The Secretary for Security, Mr Tang Ping-keung, visited the venue and met with participants to learn about their views on the port and experiences of the visit today. He was pleased to note that many participants responded positively and were looking forward to the early opening of the redeveloped Huanggang Port, which would bring a more efficient and convenient clearance experience to the public. Mr Tang also distributed gift packs prepared by the Security Bureau and took photographs with participants.

     The community experience day was conducted in a positive and enthusiastic atmosphere, with many participants expressing excitement about the event. The event effectively enhanced participants' understanding of the public transport arrangements, immigration and customs clearance, and passenger-friendly facilities at the port building. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will continue to work closely with the Shenzhen side to prepare comprehensively for the opening of the port.

item.title: CE congratulates Hong Kong, China athletes for achievements at 20th Asian Games
item.description:
The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, today (October 4) congratulated the Hong Kong, China delegation on their outstanding achievements at the 20th Asian Games, and commended Hong Kong, China athletes for demonstrating their perseverance and exceptional prowess in the competitions.

     Mr Lee said, "The Hong Kong, China delegation consisted of some 580 athletes competing in 38 events at this Asian Games. All the participating athletes have given their utmost in every competition. They have won a total of 54 medals, comprising 11 gold medals, 19 silver medals and 24 bronze medals - surpassing previous record for the total number of medals while also securing the most gold medals ever, marking an encouraging achievement, demonstrating Hong Kong, China athletes' perseverance and standards of excellence that have brought honour to both the country and Hong Kong.

     "Hong Kong, China athletes won gold medals in wushu, swimming, rowing, squash, sailing, tennis, windsurfing, and rugby sevens. Among them, the squash team, the sailing team and the tennis team achieved historic results, writing a glorious chapter for Hong Kong sports. The courage, relentless spirit, perseverance and unyielding determination shown by Hong Kong, China athletes on the field of play are the finest embodiment of the Hong Kong spirit. I believe all Hong Kong people share my excitement and immense pride in their excellent performances.

     "Hong Kong, China athletes have once again achieved excellent results at this latest edition of the Asian Games, demonstrating that the Government's policies and its strategic resource support are on the right track. I also extend my heartfelt gratitude to the Hong Kong Sports Institute (HKSI), the Sports Federation & Olympic Committee of Hong Kong, China, the various national sports associations and the coaching and medical teams for their unwavering support and dedication to nurturing our athletes over the years. I look forward to extending my congratulations to the athletes in person at the commendation ceremony to be held in due course.

     "The current-term Government is proactively promoting sports development and continuously developing elite sports, with various measures implemented to enhance the quality of training and support for elite athletes. This comprehensive support includes the hardware facilities of the HKSI, training resources, and research and development of sports medicine and sports science. In the 2024 Policy Address, I proposed to review the mechanism of direct financial support for elite athletes. The grant level of direct financial support for them has been comprehensively increased from April 1, 2025, and the subsidy ceiling of athletes' participation in competitions has also been raised this year. We will continue to provide full support for Hong Kong, China athletes to excel at international and regional competitions, and to take Hong Kong sport to a new level."

item.title: Buildings Department investigating incident involving quality of steel reinforcement in a house at One Stanley
item.description:
With regard to a media report concerning the quality of steel reinforcement in a house at One Stanley in Stanley, the Buildings Department (BD) is highly concerned about the incident and has been following it up seriously and conducting investigation upon receiving the report. If any building professionals and contractors are found to have violated the Buildings Ordinance (BO) after investigation, the BD will pursue the matter seriously, including instigating prosecutions and/or disciplinary actions.

     The occupation permit of the house was issued in July 2023. The owner is carrying out decoration works after purchasing the house. The BD received a report in January this year from the owner's representative regarding the structural safety of the floor slabs in the house. After making an appointment with the owner, staff of the BD was arranged to carry out an on-site inspection in March and considered that the overall structure of the house posed no obvious danger. The BD then launched an investigation into the case and also wrote to the registered structural engineer of the development, requesting a report and relevant information, including test reports and certificates for the materials concerned.

     The BD deployed its staff to the house several times between June and September to carry out inspections, tests and examinations. These included rebound hammer test on concrete strength, cover-meter survey, surface penetrating radar survey for checking alignment of reinforcement, concrete core compressive strength test, as well as on-site open-up inspections. The BD is currently analysing the data obtained from these tests and examinations. It is found that the concrete cover of one of the beams at the ground floor is not installed with wire mesh as required by the approved plan, and the steel reinforcement of some slabs deviated from the approved plan. Although such situations will not pose obvious danger, the BD considers that the quality of works warrants concerns and follow-up actions. The BD will conduct further investigation and has written to the relevant parties, including the authorized person, the registered structural engineer, the registered contractor and the developer of the development, requesting interviews to assist in the investigation and to provide information.

     The BD reminded the industry that under the BO, building professionals (including structural engineers) and contractors must supervise and carry out building works in accordance with the approved plans. Building professionals or contractors are subject to prosecutions and/or disciplinary actions if they are found to have failed to properly supervise or carry out building works during the BD's audits and/or upon receiving complaints. The Development Bureau will submit a bill to the Legislative Council by the end of this year to amend the BO, which will also include increasing penalties of the relevant provisions.

item.title: Singapore ETO supports Hong Kong harmonica virtuoso CY Leo's concert and music exchanges in Singapore (with photos)
item.description:
​The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Singapore (Singapore ETO), with funding provided by the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau, supported the Hong Kong harmonica virtuoso and two-time solo harmonica world champion CY Leo (Ho Cheuk-yin) in presenting a series of music and cultural exchange activities in Singapore from October 2 to 4 as part of his Asia Tour 2026. 

     The highlight of the Singapore programme was the "Two Worlds in One" concert at the Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay this evening (October 3), which drew an audience of over 200 and was warmly received. The Singapore ETO invited guests from across the Singapore community, including representatives of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Public of Singapore, business associations, cultural organisations and the local Hong Kong community.

     Led by Leo on harmonica, the performance featured Hong Kong guest singer Ashley Lin, Hong Kong musician Daniel Chu on piano and keyboards, Korean musicians Jongkuk Kim on drums and Jaeshin Park on electric bass. The programme featured a range of works including "Forgiveness", "Bewildered Heart", "A Mantra Samba", "Two Worlds" and "New Beginnings".

     Upon completion of the performance, the Director of the Singapore ETO, Ms Elsa Hung, met Leo and the other performers to show her support and encouragement ahead of the concert. Ms Hung encouraged them to make full use of the opportunity to connect with local audiences and fellow musicians, and to showcase Hong Kong's creativity and cultural vibrancy through their exchanges in Singapore.

     The Singapore ETO's support for the tour forms part of its ongoing efforts to bring Hong Kong's arts and cultural talent to wider audiences in Southeast Asia, create opportunities for Hong Kong artists to connect with overseas audiences and industry counterparts, and foster closer cultural and people-to-people exchanges. These efforts also contribute to Hong Kong's development as an East-meets-West centre for international arts and cultural exchanges.

     The Singapore stop was organised in collaboration with Harmonica Aficionados Society (Singapore) (HAS), with side activities arranged to deepen exchanges with the local harmonica community. On October 2, Leo conducted a workshop entitled "The Bottleneck in the Study of Chromatic Harmonica" for around 40 local harmonica enthusiasts. On October 4, he will give a guest performance at the HAS's "Qin Yuan 51: A Tapestry of Harmonics" at the Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay.

     "Two Worlds in One" concert is a musical project initiated by Leo that explores the possibilities of the harmonica through jazz, pop and world music. The Asia tour includes stops in Taipei, Penang and Seoul. The Singapore concert also featured local harmonica groups and ensemble performances alongside Leo and his touring musicians, showcasing Hong Kong's musical talent overseas while fostering exchanges and collaboration between musicians from Hong Kong and Singapore.

item.title: CHP records case of severe paediatric influenza infection
item.description:
​​The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 3) recorded a severe paediatric influenza infection case. The CHP urged the public to receive vaccinations as early as possible to safeguard their own health and that of their families. In addition, the public should maintain good personal and environmental hygiene at all times to prevent influenza and other respiratory illnesses.

     The case involves a nine-year-old girl with underlying illnesses. She developed a fever on September 30. On October 1, she developed a cough and vomiting, and was taken to a private clinic. On the same day, she was referred to the Accident and Emergency Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital, where she was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of the hospital for treatment. Her respiratory specimen tested positive for influenza B virus. Her clinical diagnosis was influenza B infection complicated with septic shock and severe pneumonia. The patient remains hospitalised at the PICU in critical condition.

     The CHP's preliminary investigation revealed that the patient had no travel history during the incubation period, and has not received the 2026/27 Seasonal Influenza Vaccination (SIV). The investigation also revealed that two of her household contacts had developed mild fever and upper respiratory symptoms recently, but both have now recovered. The CHP will continue to investigate the case.

     Hong Kong entered the influenza season in late June. The latest surveillance data showed that influenza activity remains at a high level. Since the end of June, a cumulative total of 21 cases of severe paediatric influenza infection have been recorded. Among these cases, 16 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospital, two patients are in stable condition, two are in critical condition and one has passed away. Due to widespread influenza transmission in the community in recent months, there has been a significant increase in both the number of infections and severe cases. With the start of the new school year and an increase in group activities, the CHP anticipates that influenza activity will remain at a high level in the coming weeks while influenza outbreaks in schools are expected to increase. Therefore, schools and parents must remain vigilant and take preventive measures.

     The 2026/27 SIV Programmes, including the SIV School Outreach Programme (SIVSOP), commenced on September 17. The SIVSOP this year has introduced a new Electronic Consent Form (e-consent form) feature via eHealth. This new measure not only facilitates the public to join the SIV Programmes but also streamlines the administrative procedures for healthcare service providers and schools, so that SIV outreach activities can start as early as possible. Approximately 100 schools have organised SIV outreach activities, a significant increase compared to the same period last year. SIV outreach activities are expected to be completed by mid-December, about two weeks earlier than last year. The CHP appeals to all schools and parents in Hong Kong to work closely with the CHP and complete the consent process as soon as possible, so that students can be arranged to receive SIV earlier.

     The CHP reminds parents that the health condition of children with influenza can deteriorate rapidly. Parents must pay close attention to their condition, and visit an accident and emergency department immediately if the child's condition deteriorates with symptoms such as shortness of breath, wheezing, blue lips, chest pain, confusion, a persistent fever or convulsions. Members of the public should seek medical attention as soon as possible if they develop respiratory symptoms. If they live with members of high-risk groups, such as children, the elderly and those with underlying illnesses or compromised immune systems, they should wear a surgical mask at home to reduce the risk of infecting them. Other effective ways to reduce the spread of the disease include maintaining household hygiene, frequently cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces, practising good hand hygiene, and ensuring proper indoor air circulation.

     Members of the public may refer to the CHP's COVID-19 & Flu Express, Seasonal Influenza Webpage and Vaccination Schemes for the latest information.

item.title: CSD holds Inauguration Ceremony for Honorary Advisory Committee of Correctional Services Pioneer Leaders and Trainees Promotion Ceremony (with photos)
item.description:
The Correctional Services Department (CSD) today (October 3) held the Inauguration Ceremony for the Honorary Advisory Committee of the Correctional Services Pioneer Leaders (CSPL) and Trainees Promotion Ceremony to appoint new committee members and commend outstanding trainees.

     The Commissioner of Correctional Services, Mr Wong Kwok-hing, officiated at the ceremony. Other guests included members of the CSPL Honorary Advisory Committee and representatives from schools participating in the school-based CSPL programme. More than 100 trainees and their family members attended.

     To support the long-term development of the CSPL, the CSD appointed eight distinguished individuals from different sectors of society as new members of the CSPL Honorary Advisory Committee this year. They will inject new momentum into the youth uniformed group, driving the group toward continuous development.

     Moreover, the CSD also hosted a promotion ceremony for CSPL trainees today. With their outstanding performances, 79 trainees were promoted this year following the completion of stringent assessments. Among them, three were promoted to Senior Leaders, 11 were promoted to Intermediate Leaders, and 65 were promoted to Advanced Leaders. Mr Wong extended his congratulations to the promoted trainees and encouraged them to pass on their knowledge and experiences to new trainees, guiding them in their collective development, fostering team spirit, and contributing to society.

     In his speech, Mr Wong noted that since the launch of the Captain Gor Union in December 2024, with Captain Gor being the mascot of the CSPL, the Department has been recruiting primary and secondary school students as non-uniformed group members. The Captain Gor Union aims to nurture a new generation of young people with an affection for the country and Hong Kong and a positive mindset, in a systematic manner through a wide range of activities. It will also enable the CSD to recruit young people with potential to join the CSPL to inject new blood into the team. The new website of the Captain Gor Union was officially launched last month, providing a one-stop platform for youth and education-related organisations to access the latest information and enrol in various community education activities at any time.

     At the ceremony, CSPL trainees shared their experiences from participating in the programme. They mentioned that the training broadened their horizons and helped them discover their potential. They aspired to actively give back to society, promote the values of inclusiveness and being law-abiding, and work together to build a better Hong Kong.

     The CSD will continue to disseminate to young people the messages of safeguarding the country and home, leading a law-abiding and drug-free life as well as supporting offender rehabilitation through diverse activities.

item.title: Employers, contractors and employees should be aware of electrical safety at work during rainstorms
item.description:

     A spokesman for the LD said today (October 3) that employers and contractors should avoid assigning employees to carry out electrical work (such as electric arc welding work) or handle electrical plant at places affected by rainstorms, and should refer to the "Code of Practice in Times of Adverse Weather and 'Extreme Conditions'" and the "Guide on Safety at Work in times of Inclement Weather" issued by the LD.

(ii) Before carrying out any electrical work or handling any electrical plant, cut off and lock out the power supply source, then test the circuit concerned to confirm that it is dead and display suitable warning notices, and issue a work permit thereafter;

(iii) Ensure that protective devices (such as suitable and adequate fuses and circuit breakers) for the electrical installations or electrical plant have been installed and maintained in good working order, and portable electric tools must be double-insulated or properly earthed;

(iv) Provide suitable personal protective equipment such as insulating gloves and insulating mats for employees; and

(v) If live electrical work is unavoidable, a comprehensive risk assessment should be conducted by a competent person and the appropriate safety precautions should be taken to remove or properly control the electrical hazards involved before such work can proceed.

     In addition, employees should co-operate with the employer or contractor to follow the safety instructions and use the safety equipment provided.

     The LD has published guidebooks and leaflets on electrical work safety. These safety publications are available free from divisional offices of the department or can be downloaded from its website (www.labour.gov.hk/eng/public/content2_8.htm).

The Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law, today (October 2) extended her congratulations to sailing athletes Kiu Ethan Lachlan, Polson Louis Oliver, Chloe Kong and Mccarley Wong on winning two gold medals for the Hong Kong, China Delegation in Boys' Skiff - 29er and Girls' Skiff - 29er respectively at the 20th Asian Games.

     Miss Law also extended her congratulations to squash athletes Chan Sin-yuk, Ho Tze-lok, Lee Ka-yi and Tse Yee-lam, Toby for winning a silver medal in Women's Team; sailing athlete Nicholas Bezy Halliday for winning a silver medal in Men's Dinghy ILCA7; track cycling athlete Lee Sze-wing for winning a bronze medal in Women's Omnium; and tennis athletes Eudice Chong and Wong Hong-yi for winning a bronze medal in Women's Doubles.

     Miss Law said, "Hong Kong, China athletes had a great day in sailing event today. Kiu Ethan Lachlan, Polson Louis Oliver, Chloe Kong and Mccarley Wong were in excellent form, winning two gold medals respectively in the Boys' Skiff - 29er and Girls' Skiff - 29er. This marks Hong Kong, China's first-ever gold medals in sailing event. Nicholas Bezy Halliday also performed admirably, winning a silver medal. At this year's Asian Games, Hong Kong, China sailing athletes have won a total of two gold medals, two silver medals, and one bronze medal, marking a new milestone in the history of Hong Kong sailing sports."

     "Also, Chan Sin-yuk, Ho Tze-lok, Lee Ka-yi and Tse Yee-lam, Toby battled their opponents to win silver medals for two consecutive times; Lee Sze-wing gave her all on the cycling track, winning a bronze medal in the individual event after winning a silver medal at the Women's Madison yesterday (October 1); Eudice Chong and Wong Hong-yi performed to their best, winning a medal in the Women's Doubles. item.title: Hong Kong Customs arrests director of yoga centre suspected of engaging in unfair trade practices in sale of services
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs today (October 2) arrested a male director of a chain yoga centre suspected of wrongly accepting payments when selling services, in contravention of the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (TDO).

     Customs earlier received information alleging that the yoga centre suddenly announced the business suspension of its all branches and failed to provide prepaid services purchased by customers. Customs officers immediately conducted an investigation and found that the yoga centre still accepted payments from customers before the announcement of its business suspension. Customers who had purchased prepaid yoga or fitness courses were unable to use the services concerned.

     After a follow-up investigation, Customs officers today conducted enforcement operations and arrested a 61-year-old male director of the company. The investigation is ongoing.

     Customs has been paying close attention to the case and called on members of the public affected to provide information. As of 5pm today, Customs had received a total of 381 complaints, involving contracts amounting to about $4.07 million.

     Customs reminds traders to comply with the requirements of the TDO. Consumers are also reminded to procure services at reputable shops and think prudently before making consumption decisions with prepayments. After purchasing services, they should keep the relevant records, such as transaction receipts and contracts, which can become basic information in case a complaint is lodged in the future.

     Under the TDO, any trader commits an offence if at the time of acceptance of payment, the trader intends not to supply the product or intends to supply a materially different product, or there are no reasonable grounds for believing that the trader will be able to supply the product within a specified or reasonable period. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for five years.
     ​
     Members of the public may report any suspected violations of the TDO to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Government holds Learning Outcomes Sharing Session of "Salute to the National Flag" Beijing Visit Delegation to promote outcomes of the activity among young people and all sectors of society (with photos/video)
item.description:
To further consolidate and deepen the educational effectiveness of the "Salute to the National Flag" Hong Kong and Macao Youth Flag-Raising Teams' Beijing Visit Delegation, the Education Bureau today (October 2) held a learning outcomes sharing session of the delegation at Kowloon Technical School. About 250 student representatives of the delegation from tertiary institutions, secondary and primary schools shared what they had seen, heard and felt during the five-day visit to Beijing, with a view to promote the outcomes of the activity among more young people and various sectors of the society. In particular, the session brought to a wider audience the cordial remarks and exhortations of President Xi and the Central Government to Hong Kong and Macao young people, conveyed by Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council, Mr Ding Xuexiang, when he received the delegation at the Great Hall of the People, with the aim of continuously promoting patriotic education in schools and the community.

     The session was officiated by the Chief Secretary for Administration, Mr Chan Kwok-ki. The Secretary for Education, Dr Choi Yuk-lin; the Director-General of the Education and Youth Department of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), Dr Wang Weiming; the Convenor of the Working Group on Patriotic Education, Dr Eliza Chan; the Director of the Association of Hong Kong Flag-guards, Mr Ng Wun-kit; and the Chairman of the Hong Kong Army Cadets Association, Dr Bunny Chan, were also in attendance.

     Speaking at the session, Mr Chan said that the delegation was a high-level "walking classroom", enabling students, through the solemn flag-raising ceremony at Tiananmen Square, to feel for themselves the national dignity represented by the national flag and the national anthem, deepen their understanding of the symbolic meaning of the national flag, and strengthen their sense of national identity and patriotism. From the country's millennia-old cultural heritage to the development achievements of the new era, students experienced at first hand our country's journey from arduous struggle to the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

     He said, "What is even more remarkable is that the delegation was received in person by Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council, Mr Ding Xuexiang, and the Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Work Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council, Mr Xia Baolong, at the Great Hall of the People. Vice Premier Ding conveyed the cordial remarks and exhortations of President Xi and the Central Government to the young people from Hong Kong and Macao, enabling students to feel the care and expectations of the Central Authorities for Hong Kong and Macao young people, and to understand more deeply the important meaning carried by the national flag."

     Mr Chan emphasised that patriotic education has all along been a top priority of the work of the HKSAR Government. Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the 2026 Policy Address, both released in the middle of last month, also list the promotion of patriotic education as a key task. And today's learning outcomes sharing session aims to pass on more widely and further what the students learned in Beijing, so that more young people may gain a deeper understanding of the important meaning of the national flag and feel more deeply our country's care and concern for young people. The Government will continue to join hands with various sectors of the society and, through rich and diverse means, enable young people to build a firm sense of national identity, national confidence and a sense of responsibility through first-hand experience. 

     Today's sharing session began with a flag-raising ceremony. A joint team formed by flag-raising teams of the Association of Hong Kong Flag-guards and the Hong Kong Army Cadets Association, drawing on the experience of exchanges and interaction in Beijing with the People's Liberation Army Ceremonial Escort Battalion, conducted a solemn flag-raising ceremony. Booths were also set up at the session for members of the delegation to introduce their learning experience in Beijing.
     ​
     The "Salute to the National Flag" Delegation conducted its thematic activity in Beijing from September 18 to 22. About 1 200 flag-raising team representatives, teachers, students and youth group representatives from Hong Kong and Macao took part. The visit aimed to enable participating students to witness in person the solemn flag-raising ceremony at Tiananmen Square and experience the historical culture of the capital and our country's development achievements, to combine what they felt at first hand with what they had learned in class, to deepen their sense of national identity and patriotism, and to take root the spirit and sentiment of patriotism in the hearts of young people.

item.title: CCIDA sponsors industry participation in China International Comics Festival Expo (with photos)
item.description:
The Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency (CCIDA) under the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau sponsored the Hong Kong Digital Entertainment Association to lead an industry delegation to participate in the China International Comics Festival Expo (CICF Expo) held in Guangzhou from today (October 2) to October 5. The Hong Kong Pavilion is set up at the CICF Expo to showcase art toys, games, animation, comics, as well as merchandise and spin-offs derived from cultural intellectual properties (IPs), fully demonstrating the creative capabilities and commercial potential of Hong Kong's digital entertainment industry.
      
     This marks the second consecutive year that CCIDA sponsors the project, with a total of 16 Hong Kong enterprises participating this year. The Hong Kong Pavilion, themed "Designer Toy, Game, Animation and Comics", features a range of immersive and interactive experiences, including stage interactions with original IP characters, game demos, and live drawing sessions by renowned comic artists. The pavilion also introduces for the first time a smart guide system to enhance visitors' experience, allowing them to easily access information on company profiles, project backgrounds, creative concepts and key highlights. By participating in the CICF Expo, the Hong Kong industry not only showcases its diverse creative capabilities but also actively promotes its works to the Greater Bay Area, bridging creative resources and achieving complementary industrial strengths between the Hong Kong and Chinese Mainland markets.
      
     As one of the most prestigious and influential animation and game exhibitions in the Greater Bay Area, the CICF Expo is expected to showcase over 1 000 brands with over 7 000 types of merchandise this year, attracting over 450 000 visits and interactive engagements on-site. For more information about the CICF Expo and the Hong Kong Pavilion, please visit www.cicfexpo.com and www.hkdea.org.

item.title: CHP investigates cluster of Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae carrier cases
item.description:
​The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health is today (October 2) investigating a cluster of Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) carrier cases involving five residents of a residential care home for the elderly (RCHE). The CHP reminded all RCHEs to implement measures for the prevention and control of infectious diseases in accordance with the Guidelines on Prevention of Communicable Disease in RCHEs (the Guidelines).
 
     The CHP recently received a notification from the Hospital Authority (HA) that three residents living on the same floor of an RCHE in North Point had been admitted to a public hospital for treatment due to their underlying illnesses. Their admission screening samples tested positive for CPE upon laboratory testing and they were suspected to have been infected in the RCHE. The CHP immediately conducted epidemiological investigations, contact tracing and screening. Subsequently, the CHP identified two additional carrier cases at the RCHE. All five patients (three males and two females, aged 77 to 92) are carriers. None of them exhibited symptoms associated with CPE infection. They are currently in stable condition.
 
     The CHP's investigation found that the source of infection for the aforementioned five carrier cases may have been another previously identified CPE carrier case on the same floor of the same RCHE. After inspecting the facility, CHP staff discovered that the RCHE had not duly implemented relevant infection prevention and control measures. It cannot be ruled out that the bacteria were transmitted within the RCHE via staff, or contaminated environment and objects. The CHP reminded the staff of the RCHE to adhere to the Guidelines and take necessary measures, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment, enhancing hand hygiene among staff and residents, and thoroughly cleaning and disinfecting the environment and objects. The CHP also recommended that the RCHE cohort the carriers in a single designated area.
 
     The CHP will continue to investigate the cluster of cases and conduct screening at the RCHE concerned to determine whether there are any other CPE-carriers. The CHP will also continue to put the RCHE under medical surveillance.
 
     Enterobacteriaceae (such as Escherichia coli and Klebsiella) are common pathogens that can cause infections in various parts of the body, including urinary tract infections, intra-abdominal infections or blood infection. CPE are enterobacteriaceae that produce carbapenemase, an enzyme that can deactivate carbapenems and other beta-lactam antibiotics such as penicillins. These bacteria are commonly resistant to multiple antibiotics, limiting therapeutic options, and may render severe clinical infections difficult to treat. The range of diseases associated with CPE varies from asymptomatic carriage to potentially life-threatening or fatal infections. The level of risk depends on which part of the body is affected by the infection and the patient's general health.

     The proper use of antibiotics and maintaining good personal and environmental hygiene, especially hand hygiene, are important for preventing the emergence and cross-transmission of multi-drug resistant organisms (MDROs), such as CPE. In addition, susceptible individuals such as the elderly, infants, young children, people with weakened immunity and pregnant women can reduce their risk of contracting MDROs by avoiding raw or undercooked foods.

item.title: Police appeal for information on fatal traffic accident in Western District
item.description:
Police today (October 2) appealed to the public for information on a fatal traffic accident in Western District yesterday (October 1) in which a man died.
Police received a report at about 10.31pm yesterday, a private car driven by a man was travelling along Mount Davis Path towards Victoria Road. When approaching the junction of Victoria Road and Mount Davis Path, it reportedly collided with a motorcycle driven by another man travelling along Victoria Road southbound.
Sustaining serious head injury, the 63-year-old male motorcyclist was rushed to Queen Mary Hospital in unconscious state and was certified dead at 9.46am today (October 2).
The 50-year-old male private car driver, who is an off-duty auxiliary police officer, was arrested for dangerous driving causing death. He has been released on bail pending further enquiries and is required to report back to Police in early November.
Investigation by the Special Investigation Team of Traffic, Hong Kong Island is underway.
Anyone who witnessed the accident or has any information to offer is urged to contact the investigating officers on 3660 6848.

item.title: Government reaches settlement arrangement with MTRCL on Hong Kong Section of Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link project and Shatin to Central Link project
item.description:
The Government today (October 2) reached a settlement arrangement with the MTR Corporation Limited (MTRCL) on the Hong Kong Section of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link (XRL) project and the Shatin to Central Link (SCL) project.

     The XRL and SCL are railway projects implemented by the MTRCL under entrustment from the Government. Following the dispute resolution approach specified under the entrustment agreements for the two projects, the Government and the MTRCL conducted multiple rounds of negotiations, and reached a settlement arrangement today. In relation to the programme delay in the construction of the XRL project, the MTRCL will pay HK$2.25 billion to the Government. On the other hand, in respect of disputes relating to the SCL project, the MTRCL has in the past proactively shouldered the additional project management cost (PMC) for the whole project and additional costs arising from the quality incident of the Hung Hom Station Extension (HUH Incident), totalling approximately HK$2.8 billion. Both parties have agreed not to pursue any claims against each other for the delay of the SCL project. The settlement arrangement has fully taken into account the responsibilities of the MTRCL on the programme delays of the two projects.

     A spokesman for the Transport and Logistics Bureau said, "The Government has been following up in a serious, rigorous and professional manner with the MTRCL on its responsibilities as the project manager in respect of programme delays in the construction of the XRL and SCL projects, in order to safeguard the legitimate interests of the Government and the public. Under the mutually agreed dispute resolution approach, personnel from both the Government and the MTRCL organised and analysed a substantial volume of materials, and fully consulted independent and professional engineering and legal advice in the process to clarify the liability issues involved. The two sides engaged in multiple rounds of discussions, working proactively to resolve the disputes and successfully reaching a consensus in the end.

     "Following the programme delays of the XRL and SCL projects, the Government and the MTRCL have thoroughly reflected on the experiences, and put in place a series of enhancements to strengthen the governance, monitoring and cost management mechanisms of railway projects over the past few years, with a view to further improving the oversight of project management and process at the institutional level. The Government and the MTRCL have also implemented the enhanced mechanisms in railway projects currently under way, including Kwu Tung Station, Tung Chung Line Extension, Oyster Bay Station, Tuen Mun South Extension, Hung Shui Kiu Station and the Northern Link Project. The Government will continue to closely monitor the progress and delivery performance of railway projects, and urge the MTRCL to implement new railway projects on schedule and within budget. At the same time, in accordance with the project agreements for the aforementioned new railway projects, the MTRCL is required to bear all construction and operational risks associated with the new railway projects, including the risk of project cost overruns," the spokesman added.

     The XRL and the SCL are railways funded and owned by the Government, which has entrusted the MTRCL with the design, construction, testing and commissioning of the projects. Construction of the XRL commenced in 2010, and was originally scheduled for commissioning in August 2015. Due to programme delay and cost overruns, the Government and the MTRCL signed a definitive agreement in 2015, agreeing to extend the Programme to Complete to the third quarter of 2018, and increase the estimated Cost to Complete (CTC) by HK$19.42 billion from HK$65 billion to HK$84.42 billion, which is then capped at this level. In November 2015, prior to the Government's application to the Legislative Council (LegCo) for additional funding, the MTRCL announced the distribution of a special dividend to its shareholders. The Government, as the MTRCL's major shareholder, received a total amount of HK$19.51 billion in special dividend. The XRL formally commenced operation in September 2018.

     Construction of the SCL commenced in 2012. The Tai Wai to Hung Hom Section (linking the Ma On Shan Line and the West Rail Line to form the Tuen Ma Line) was originally scheduled for commissioning in December 2018, while the Cross-harbour Extension (extending from Hung Hom to the Wan Chai Exhibition Centre and Admiralty) was originally scheduled for commissioning in December 2020. Due to a series of events, including the archaeological discoveries at Sung Wong Toi Station, wartime bombs uncovered at the Exhibition Centre Station site, unforeseen ground conditions, and the HUH Incident, the Tuen Ma Line was eventually fully commissioned in June 2021, while the Cross-harbour Extension commenced operation in May 2022. The estimated CTC also increased from HK$79.82 billion to HK$90.73 billion (the additional funding of HK$10.91 billion sought from the LegCo at that time did not include the additional PMC for the whole project and additional costs arising from the HUH Incident totalling approximately HK$2.8 billion, which the MTRCL proactively shouldered).

item.title: Incoming passenger convicted and jailed for possession of duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photo)
item.description:
An incoming female passenger was sentenced to four weeks' imprisonment with a fine of $1,500 by the Fanling Magistrates' Courts today (October 2) for possessing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO).
      
     Customs officers intercepted an incoming 55-year-old Mainland female passenger at the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line Control Point yesterday (October 1) and seized 2 381 duty-not-paid cigarettes from her personal belongings, with an estimated market value of about $11,000, and a duty potential of about $7,800. The female passenger was subsequently arrested.
      
     Customs welcomes the sentences, noting that even a first-time offender may still be imprisoned. The custodial sentence has imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflects the seriousness of the offences. Members of the public should not defy the law.
      
     Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.
      
     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Incoming passenger convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and alternative smoking products (with photo)
item.description:
An incoming male passenger was sentenced to six months' imprisonment and fined $1,500 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (October 2) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes, failing to declare them to Customs officers, as well as importing alternative smoking products, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO) and the Import and Export Ordinance (IEO).

     Customs officers intercepted a 45-year-old incoming Mainland male passenger arriving in Hong Kong from Tokyo, Japan, at Hong Kong International Airport on September 30 and seized 7 008 duty-not-paid cigarettes and 40 000 alternative smoking products, with an estimated market value of about $235,000 and a duty potential of about $23,000, from his personal baggage. The passenger was subsequently arrested.

     Customs welcomes the sentence. The custodial sentence has imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflects the seriousness of the offences.

     Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, tobacco products are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys duty-not-paid tobacco commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Under the IEO, any person who imports an alternative smoking product into Hong Kong commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Employers, contractors and employees should be aware of electrical safety at work during rainstorms
item.description:
As the rainstorm warning has been issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, the Labour Department (LD) reminds employers and contractors that they should adopt necessary work arrangements and take suitable safety measures to protect the safety of their employees when they are carrying out electrical work or handling electrical plant.

     A spokesman for the LD said today (October 2) that employers and contractors should avoid assigning employees to carry out electrical work (such as electric arc welding work) or handle electrical plant at places affected by rainstorms, and should refer to the "Code of Practice in Times of Adverse Weather and 'Extreme Conditions'" and the "Guide on Safety at Work in times of Inclement Weather" issued by the LD.

     Even if electrical work is carried out or electrical plant is handled at places not affected by a rainstorm, suitable safety measures must still be adopted to prevent an electric shock as the air would be more humid. Such measures include:

(i) Ensure that all live parts of an electrical installation are isolated from the power supply source and rendered dead, and the isolation from the power supply source must be maintained as long as electrical work is being carried out;

(ii) Before carrying out any electrical work or handling any electrical plant, cut off and lock out the power supply source, then test the circuit concerned to confirm that it is dead and display suitable warning notices, and issue a work permit thereafter;

(iii) Ensure that protective devices (such as suitable and adequate fuses and circuit breakers) for the electrical installations or electrical plant have been installed and maintained in good working order, and portable electric tools must be double-insulated or properly earthed;

(iv) Provide suitable personal protective equipment such as insulating gloves and insulating mats for employees; and

(v) If live electrical work is unavoidable, a comprehensive risk assessment should be conducted by a competent person and the appropriate safety precautions should be taken to remove or properly control the electrical hazards involved before such work can proceed.

     In addition, employees should co-operate with the employer or contractor to follow the safety instructions and use the safety equipment provided.

     The LD has published guidebooks and leaflets on electrical work safety. These safety publications are available free from divisional offices of the department or can be downloaded from its website (www.labour.gov.hk/eng/public/content2_8.htm).

     Should there be any questions about occupational safety and health matters, please contact the Occupational Safety Officer of the LD at 2559 2297.

item.title: Update on mosquito-borne diseases, dengue fever and chikungunya fever
item.description:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 2) announced the latest situation regarding dengue fever (DF) and chikungunya fever (CF). Although Hong Kong has entered autumn, the weather has yet to cool down and the rainy season has not yet ended, thus favourable for mosquito breeding. Members of the public are reminded to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases.
     
Dengue fever
----------------

     From September 25 to yesterday (October 1), no new cases of DF had been recorded. Hong Kong has recorded 32 DF cases so far this year, comprising 30 imported cases and two local cases. A total of 59 DF cases were recorded last year (2025), all of which were imported cases. In 2024, 161 DF cases were recorded, comprising 156 imported cases and five local cases.
          
     According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the global incidence of DF has markedly increased over the past two decades, posing a substantial public health challenge. In 2024, the WHO recorded over 14 million DF cases, which was a record number. In 2025, over five million cases and over 4 000 DF-related deaths were reported in over 90 countries/territories. From January to August 2026, around 2.2 million cases and over 1 000 DF-related deaths have been recorded globally.

      DF has long been prevalent in many neighbouring tourist destinations. So far this year, Sri Lanka and Vietnam each recorded over 100 000 cases; Bangladesh and Cambodia each recorded over 80 000 cases; Indonesia and Malaysia each recorded over 70 000 cases; and Singapore recorded over 2 500 cases. Meanwhile, according to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of August 31, 2026, Guangdong Province has recorded 431 cases, of which 150 were recorded in August.

     Detailed information on the latest DF situation in Hong Kong, as well as neighbouring and overseas countries and areas, has been uploaded to the CHP's website.
 
Chikungunya fever
-----------------------

     From September 25 to yesterday, the CHP recorded one imported CF case, involving a 62-year-old female. The patient had visited Guangdong Province during the incubation period. The CHP considered that she was infected during travel. The case was classified as an imported case. The patient has been admitted to the hospital for treatment in a mosquito-free environment and is in stable condition. She has two household contacts who are currently asymptomatic and under medical surveillance. The CHP's epidemiological investigation is ongoing. The case has been reported to the health authority of Guangdong Province.
 
     Hong Kong has recorded four confirmed CF cases so far this year, including three imported cases and one local case. Hong Kong recorded a total of 82 confirmed CF cases last year. Among them, 11 were local cases and the rest were imported cases.

     According to the WHO, a total of 502 264 CF cases and 186 CF-related deaths were reported in 41 countries/territories last year. Cases were reported in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe. According to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of August 31, 2026, Guangdong Province has recorded 739 cases, with 496 recorded in August, a sharp increase from the 36 and 171 cases recorded in June and July respectively.

Preventive measures to be taken by the public
----------------------------------------------------
 
     The CHP reminds members of the public to maintain good environmental hygiene, and to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Mosquito-borne diseases such as DF and CF are endemic in various countries worldwide. The risk of importation persists. Members of the public should check the situation at their destinations before travelling abroad, especially when travelling to Southeast Asian countries. Additionally, whether travelling or not, members of the public should use DEET-containing insect repellents or other effective active ingredients properly to prevent mosquito bites, but the following precautions should be taken when using them:
 
  • read the label instructions carefully first;
  • apply right before entering an area with a risk of mosquito bites;
  • apply on exposed skin and clothing;
  • use DEET of up to 30 per cent for pregnant women and up to 10 per cent for children (for children who travel to countries or areas where mosquito-borne diseases are endemic or epidemic, and where exposure is likely, those aged 2 months or above can use DEET-containing insect repellents with a DEET concentration of up to 30 per cent);
  • apply sunscreen first, then insect repellent;
  • reapply only when needed and follow the instructions; and
  • in addition to DEET, there are other insect repellents available on the market containing different active ingredients, such as IR3535 and picaridin. When using any insect repellent, the public should follow the usage instructions and precautions on the product label.
     
     ​The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) appeals to members of the public to continue to stay alert and work together to carry out mosquito prevention and control measures early, including inspecting their homes and surroundings to remove potential breeding grounds, changing water in vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces, removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week, and properly disposing of containers such as empty cans and lunch boxes. The FEHD also advises members of the public and property management agencies to keep drains free of blockage and level all defective ground surfaces to prevent the accumulation of water. They should also scrub all drains and surface sewers with an alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs.
     
     ​The public should call 1823 in case of mosquito problems, and may visit the following pages for more information: the CF page of the CHP and the Travel Health Service, the latest Travel Health News, tips for using insect repellents, and the CHP Facebook Page, Instagram Account and YouTube Channel, and also the Mosquito Prevention and Control dedicated page of the FEHD.

item.title: Import of poultry meat and products from Rural Municipality of Rockwood of Manitoba Province in Canada suspended
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (October 2) that in view of a notification from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) about an outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza in the Rural Municipality of Rockwood of Manitoba Province in Canada, the CFS has instructed the trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and products (including poultry eggs) from the area with immediate effect to protect public health in Hong Kong. 

     A CFS spokesman said that according to the Census and Statistics Department, no poultry meat and eggs were imported into Hong Kong from Canada in the first six months of this year. 

     "The CFS has contacted the Canadian authority over the issue and will closely monitor information issued by the WOAH and the relevant authorities on the avian influenza outbreak. Appropriate action will be taken in response to the development of the situation," the spokesman said.

item.title: Public urged to report flooding
item.description:

item.title: FS announces reappointment of Chief Executive Officer of Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited
item.description:
Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited (HKIC) and Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, announced today (October 2) that the HKIC Board of Directors had approved the reappointment of Ms Clara Chan as the Chief Executive Officer of the HKIC for a term of three years with effect from October 9, 2026.

     Mr Chan said, "Since taking office as the inaugural Chief Executive Officer of the HKIC in 2023, Clara has led the team in harnessing the catalytic power of 'patient capital' to mobilise capital and partners from Hong Kong, the Chinese Mainland and international markets to support the development of Hong Kong's strategic industries. She has also helped Hong Kong and Chinese Mainland companies expand into international markets through Hong Kong. The HKIC has achieved reasonable investment returns, and its achievements are widely recognised.

     "To date, the HKIC has invested in over 200 companies. Of these, 11 portfolio companies are already listed in Hong Kong, while more than 30 have submitted or plan to submit listing applications in Hong Kong this year. Every Hong Kong dollar invested by the HKIC has attracted more than eight Hong Kong dollars in international long-term market capital. Approximately 70 per cent of its portfolio companies based in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland have established or are expanding their overseas operations.

     "I look forward to Clara's continued leadership of the HKIC over the next three years, contributing to the growth of Hong Kong's financial sector, innovation and technology sector and emerging industries, while supporting the development of the Northern Metropolis and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area."

Biography of Ms Clara Chan

     Ms Chan was appointed as the inaugural Chief Executive Officer of the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited in October 2023. She has extensive experience in investment management and financial stability. Since joining the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in 2010, she has taken on several key roles, including leading the private markets team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office and advancing the development of Hong Kong's financial infrastructure and payment systems.
     ​
     Ms Chan is a barrister admitted by the High Court of Hong Kong. Earlier in her career, she joined the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government's Administrative Service, and served in different roles in policy formulation covering home affairs, cross-boundary infrastructure and financial services.

item.title: Increase in Minimum Allowable Wage and no change in food allowance for foreign domestic helpers
item.description:
The Government announced today (October 2) that the Minimum Allowable Wage (MAW) for foreign domestic helpers (FDHs) in Hong Kong will be increased by 2.35 per cent, from $5,100 to $5,220 per month.

     In addition, under the Standard Employment Contract for hiring FDHs, employers are required to provide FDHs with food free of charge. At present, the vast majority of employers provide free food to FDHs, but they may choose to pay a food allowance in lieu. The food allowance will remain unchanged at no less than $1,236 per month.

     The new MAW level will apply to all FDH contracts signed on or after tomorrow (October 3).

     A Government spokesman said, "The Government regularly reviews the MAW for FDHs to ensure its level is commensurate with Hong Kong's economic and labour market conditions, taking into account the interests of both employers and FDHs. In this year's review, we comprehensively considered a basket of socio-economic factors in accordance with the established mechanism, including Hong Kong's general economic performance and labour market conditions over the past year, near-term economic outlook, affordability of FDH employers and basic living needs of FDHs. Throughout the review process, the Government also carefully listened to the views of employers and FDHs to gain a thorough understanding of their concerns and suggestions. Having carefully assessed and balanced the views of all parties, and comprehensively considered that this year's socio-economic factors are more favourable than those at the time of last year's review, the Government has decided to suitably increase the MAW to $5,220 per month. Furthermore, the Government has reviewed the food allowance in lieu of free food and, having taken into account the relevant consumer price index, decided that the level should remain unchanged."

     FDH contracts signed today or before at the existing MAW of $5,100 per month will still be processed by the Immigration Department (ImmD), provided that the applications reach the ImmD on or before October 30 (Friday). This arrangement allows employers sufficient time to submit signed contracts to the ImmD for completion of relevant application procedures.

item.title: Provisional statistics of retail sales for August 2026
item.description:
The Census and Statistics Department (C&SD) released the latest figures on retail sales today (October 2).

     The value of total retail sales in August 2026, provisionally estimated at $32.1 billion, increased by 5.6% compared with the same month in 2025. The revised estimate of the value of total retail sales in July 2026 increased by 4.5% compared with a year earlier. For the first 8 months of 2026 taken together, it was provisionally estimated that the value of total retail sales increased by 8.5% compared with the same period in 2025.

     Of the total retail sales value in August 2026, online sales accounted for 8.7%. The value of online retail sales in that month, provisionally estimated at $2.8 billion, increased by 9.9% compared with the same month in 2025. The revised estimate of online retail sales in July 2026 increased by 9.6% compared with a year earlier. For the first 8 months of 2026 taken together, it was provisionally estimated that the value of online retail sales increased by 23.0% compared with the same period in 2025.

     After netting out the effect of price changes over the same period, the provisional estimate of the volume of total retail sales in August 2026 increased by 2.9% compared with a year earlier. The revised estimate of the volume of total retail sales in July 2026 increased by 2.4% compared with a year earlier. For the first 8 months of 2026 taken together, the provisional estimate of the total retail sales increased by 6.1% in volume compared with the same period in 2025.

     Analysed by broad type of retail outlet in descending order of the provisional estimate of the value of sales and comparing August 2026 with August 2025, the value of sales of jewellery, watches and clocks, and valuable gifts increased by 11.9%. This was followed by sales of other consumer goods not elsewhere classified (+9.6% in value); commodities in supermarkets (+2.1%); electrical goods and other consumer durable goods not elsewhere classified (+29.1%); medicines and cosmetics (+5.6%); food, alcoholic drinks and tobacco (+1.9%); books, newspapers, stationery and gifts (+11.2%); footwear, allied products and other clothing accessories (+0.6%); furniture and fixtures (+3.0%); and optical shops (+5.9%).

     On the other hand, the value of sales of wearing apparel decreased by 0.5% in August 2026 over a year earlier. This was followed by sales of commodities in department stores (-2.6% in value); motor vehicles and parts (-22.0%); fuels (-11.7%); and Chinese drugs and herbs (-6.0%).

     Based on the seasonally adjusted series, the provisional estimate of the value of total retail sales decreased by 4.6% in the three months ending August 2026 compared with the preceding three-month period, while the provisional estimate of the volume of total retail sales decreased by 3.4%.

Commentary

     A government spokesman said that total retail sales value grew at an accelerated pace of 5.6% year-on-year in August, marking the 16th consecutive month of expansion. Growth was seen across many types of retail outlets, while online retail sales value grew notably, reflecting a continued shift in consumer spending towards digital channels.

     Looking ahead, sustained economic expansion and rising labour earnings should support local consumption sentiment and spending. Continued growth in visitor arrivals and a series of upcoming mega-events should further inject vibrancy into the retail sector. The Government will continue to monitor the potential impacts of the evolving external headwinds on the local consumption market closely.

Further information

     Table 1 presents the revised figures on value index and value of retail sales for all retail outlets and by broad type of retail outlet for July 2026 as well as the provisional figures for August 2026. The provisional figures on the value of retail sales for all retail outlets and by broad type of retail outlet as well as the corresponding year-on-year changes for the first 8 months of 2026 taken together are also shown.

     Table 2 presents the revised figures on value of online retail sales for July 2026 as well as the provisional figures for August 2026. The provisional figures on year-on-year changes for the first 8 months of 2026 taken together are also shown.

     Table 3 presents the revised figures on volume index of retail sales for all retail outlets and by broad type of retail outlet for July 2026 as well as the provisional figures for August 2026. The provisional figures on year-on-year changes for the first 8 months of 2026 taken together are also shown.

     Table 4 shows the movements of the value and volume of total retail sales in terms of the year-on-year rate of change for a month compared with the same month in the preceding year based on the original series, and in terms of the rate of change for a three-month period compared with the preceding three-month period based on the seasonally adjusted series.

     The classification of retail companies follows the Hong Kong Standard Industrial Classification (HSIC) Version 2.0, which is used in various economic surveys for classifying economic units into different industry classes.

     These retail sales statistics measure the sales receipts in respect of goods sold by local retail companies and are primarily intended for gauging the short-term business performance of the local retail sector. Data on retail sales are collected from local retail companies through the Monthly Survey of Retail Sales (MRS). Local retail companies with and without physical shops are covered in MRS and their sales, both through conventional shops and online channels, are included in the retail sales statistics.

     The retail sales statistics cover consumer spending on goods but not on services (such as those on housing, catering, medical care and health services, transport and communication, financial services, education and entertainment) which account for over 50% of the overall consumer spending. Moreover, they include spending on goods in Hong Kong by visitors but exclude spending outside Hong Kong by Hong Kong residents. Hence they should not be regarded as indicators for measuring overall consumer spending.

     Users interested in the trend of overall consumer spending should refer to the data series of private consumption expenditure (PCE), which is a major component of the Gross Domestic Product published at quarterly intervals. Compiled from a wide range of data sources, PCE covers consumer spending on both goods (including goods purchased from all channels) and services by Hong Kong residents whether locally or abroad. Please refer to the C&SD publication "Gross Domestic Product by Expenditure Component" for more details.

     More detailed statistics are given in the "Report on Monthly Survey of Retail Sales". Users can browse and download this publication at the website of the C&SD (www.censtatd.gov.hk/en/EIndexbySubject.html?pcode=B1080003&scode=530).

     Users who have enquiries about the survey results may contact the Distribution Services Statistics Section of the C&SD (Tel: 3903 7400; email: mrs@censtatd.gov.hk).

item.title: Inspection of aquatic products imported from Japan
item.description:
In response to the Japanese Government's plan to discharge nuclear-contaminated water at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Station, the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene issued a Food Safety Order which prohibits all aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds originating from the 10 metropolis/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong.
 
     For other Japanese aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds that are not prohibited from being imported into Hong Kong, the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department is conducting comprehensive radiological tests to verify that the radiation levels of these products do not exceed the guideline levels before they are allowed to be supplied in the market.
 
     From noon on September 30 to noon today (October 2), the CFS conducted tests on the radiological levels of 327 food samples imported from Japan, which were of the "aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt" category. No sample was found to have exceeded the safety limit. Details can be found on the CFS's thematic website titled "Control Measures on Foods Imported from Japan" (www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_30_Nuclear_Event_and_Food_Safety.html).
 
     In parallel, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) has also tested 100 samples of local catch for radiological levels. All the samples passed the tests. Details can be found on the AFCD's website (www.afcd.gov.hk/english/fisheries/Radiological_testing/Radiological_Test.html).
 
     The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has also enhanced the environmental monitoring of the local waters. No anomaly has been detected so far. For details, please refer to the HKO's website (www.hko.gov.hk/en/radiation/monitoring/seawater.html).
 
     From August 24, 2023, to noon today, the CFS and the AFCD have conducted tests on the radiological levels of 264 429 samples of food imported from Japan (including 164 752 samples of aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt) and 56 408 samples of local catch respectively. All the samples passed the tests.

item.description:
The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) today (October 2) released the latest grading of water quality for 39 gazetted beaches (see Note 1) and one non-gazetted beach (see Note 2).
 
     Twenty beaches were rated as Good (Grade 1) and 20 as Fair (Grade 2).
 
Grade 1 beaches are:          
Cafeteria New Beach* Pui O Beach*
Cheung Chau Tung Wan Beach* Repulse Bay Beach*
Chung Hom Kok Beach Shek O Beach*

Lower Cheung Sha Beach Trio Beach*

Grade 2 beaches are:
Anglers' Beach* Hoi Mei Wan Beach*

Butterfly Beach* Kwun Yam Beach
Cafeteria Old Beach Lido Beach*
Casam Beach* Ma Wan Tung Wan Beach*
Castle Peak Beach Silver Mine Bay Beach*
Clear Water Bay Second Beach* Silverstrand Beach*
Deep Water Bay Beach* Ting Kau Beach*
Golden Beach* Turtle Cove Beach
 
     Compared with the grading released last week, Lower Cheung Sha Beach has been upgraded from Grade 2 to Grade 1. Golden Beach has been changed from Grade 1 to Grade 2.
 
     "The changes in beach water quality are generally within the normal range of natural fluctuation," an EPD spokesman said.
 
     Under the present grading system, beaches are classified into four grades, namely Good (Grade 1), Fair (Grade 2), Poor (Grade 3) and Very Poor (Grade 4), according to the level of E. coli in the water. Grades are calculated on the basis of the geometric mean of the E. coli counts on the five most recent sampling occasions.
 
     While the ratings represent the general water quality at the beaches, the EPD spokesman reminded members of the public that water quality could be temporarily affected during and after periods of heavy rain. Bathers should avoid swimming at beaches for up to three days after a tropical cyclone or heavy rainfall.
 
     A summary of beach grades is published weekly before the weekend. The latest beach grades based on the most current data may be obtained from the EPD's website on Beach Water Quality (www.epd.gov.hk/epd/beach) or the beach hotline, 2511 6666. Members of the public can also obtain the latest daily water quality forecast information for all beaches that are open for swimming through the EPD's dedicated webpage on the beach water quality forecast (www.epd.gov.hk/en/BWQForecast).
 
Note 1: Lifesaving services are provided by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department at 29 gazetted beaches, marked with an asterisk (*) above, from September 1. For details, please refer to the Leisure and Cultural Services Department's Special Announcement (www.lcsd.gov.hk/en/beach/index.html).
