item.title: HKICL alerts public of fraudulent website
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority:

     Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited (HKICL) has recently noted one fraudulent website at hkmonetaryauthority.lol purported to be from HKICL. The fraudulent website imitates as "Buyer Online Protection" to provide services including 1) refund to buyer, 2) unauthorised online transaction reporting, and 3) online transaction support, for online transaction over FPS payment. It intends to trick user into giving away personal document number and ID photo together with phone number for real name verification in order to get cash reward. In addition, it also tricks user into providing bank name, bank account number and bank account holder's name to top up and withdraw money from its platform's virtual wallet. Further, it directs user to a fraudster impersonating as customer service personnel.

     Please be reminded that the fraudulent website may have multiple combinations at the end of the link, e.g.:
  • hkmonetaryauthority.lol/page/place_an_order/?uuid=refund

     HKICL advises that this fraudulent website has no affiliation with HKICL, or any business of HKICL. HKICL will not directly provide FPS service to individual members of the public or contact individual members of the public proactively under usual circumstance. The genuine official website addresses of HKICL are www.hkicl.com.hk and fps.hkicl.com.hk. 

     HKICL urges the public to beware of suspicious calls, websites or other communications, and to remain vigilant in protecting personal information. If members of the public receive any suspicious communication purportedly from HKICL, please call HKICL’s general line at 2533 1111 to verify. Members of the public who suspect that they have become the victim of fraudulent acts should report promptly to the Police.

item.title: Hong Kong Customs seizes suspected illicit cigarettes worth about $1.88 million (with photo)
item.description:

     Customs officers on that day intercepted an incoming truck declared as carrying vegetables at the said control point. After inspection, the batch of suspected illicit cigarettes was found mix-loaded with vegetables inside 63 foam boxes on the truck. 

     A 62-year-old local male driver was arrested and the truck involved in the case was also detained. 

     An investigation is ongoing, and the arrested person has been released on bail.

     Customs will continue to take stringent enforcement action against cross-boundary smuggling activities through risk assessment and intelligence analysis.

     Customs stresses that smuggling is a serious offence. Under the Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60), any person found guilty of importing or exporting unmanifested cargo is liable to a maximum fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Moreover, under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109), any person who deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ​(crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Government proposes legislative amendments to facilitate green maritime fuel bunkering operations
item.description:
​The Government published in the Gazette today (October 2) six pieces of subsidiary legislation to amend Schedule 3 to the Pilotage Ordinance (Cap. 84) and five pieces of subsidiary legislation under the Immigration Ordinance (Cap. 115), the Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295), the Shipping and Port Control Ordinance (Cap. 313) and the Merchant Shipping (Local Vessels) Ordinance (Cap. 548) to ensure that port facilities, including anchorages, and related arrangements can meet the growing demand for green maritime fuel bunkering services amid the global trend towards maritime decarbonisation. 

     The five pieces of subsidiary legislation to be amended are:

(a) Immigration (Anchorages and Landing Places) (Amendment) Order (Cap. 115C); 
(b) Dangerous Goods (Shipping) (Amendment) Regulation 2012 (Cap. 295F);
(c) Shipping and Port Control (Amendment) Regulation (Cap. 313A);
(d) Merchant Shipping (Local Vessels) (General) (Amendment) Regulation (Cap. 548F); and 
(e) Merchant Shipping (Local Vessels) (Fees) (Amendment) Regulation (Cap. 548J). 

     A spokesman for the Transport and Logistics Bureau said, "Amid the global transition towards green shipping, the international maritime industry is accelerating the adoption of green maritime fuels to achieve maritime decarbonisation. The proposed legislative amendments will rearrange anchorages to provide additional sea room, which will increase significantly from 645 hectares to 2 877 hectares, to facilitate green maritime fuel bunkering operations. In addition, a more trade-friendly fee structure will be introduced for Government Mooring Buoys (GMBs). The amendments will offer greater convenience to vessels visiting Hong Kong for green maritime fuel bunkering in future, further consolidating Hong Kong's position as a green maritime fuel bunkering centre."

     Using green maritime fuels is the most effective way to achieve maritime decarbonisation. The Transport and Logistics Bureau promulgated the Action Plan on Green Maritime Fuel Bunkering (the Action Plan) in November 2024, setting out five strategies and 10 measures to develop Hong Kong into a green maritime fuel bunkering centre. Among them, the Action Plan proposes optimising the port layout to facilitate the mooring of green maritime fuel bunkering barges, thereby enhancing the operational flexibility of green maritime fuel bunkering.

     The proposed legislative amendments cover the optimisation of the layout of anchorages and port facilities. These include establishing seven new anchorages, adjusting the boundaries of eight anchorages, converting three dangerous goods anchorages or service anchorages into multipurpose anchorages, repealing two existing anchorages, formalising two existing recommended Traffic Separation Schemes (TSSs) into local statutory TSSs, and introducing a more trade-friendly fee structure for GMBs. These measures will ensure that the Hong Kong Port has sufficient sea room to meet the demand for green maritime fuel bunkering services. Furthermore, the Government proposes to repeal a dangerous goods anchorage and a designated bunkering area located near residential areas and to make corresponding adjustments to other anchorages and designated bunkering areas to minimise potential impacts on nearby communities.

     The Panel on Economic Development of the Legislative Council, the Pilotage Advisory Committee, the Port Operations Committee, the Local Vessels Advisory Committee, the High Speed Craft Consultative Committee, and the Dangerous Goods Standing Committee have been consulted on the legislative proposals. Relevant District Councils (including Tsuen Wan, Sham Shui Po, Kwai Tsing, Tai Po, Tuen Mun, Sai Kung, and Islands District Councils), relevant Rural Committees in the Islands District, and fishermen's representatives have also been consulted. All parties supported the proposals or raised no objection.

     The proposed amendment regulations will be submitted to the Legislative Council on October 7 for negative vetting.

item.title: Two historic buildings declared as monuments (with photos)
item.description:
The Government today (October 2) gazetted a notice announcing that the Antiquities Authority (i.e. the Secretary for Development) has declared Hung Shing Temple in Wan Chai and Stanley Mosque in Stanley as monuments under the Antiquities and Monuments Ordinance.

     Located on Queen's Road East in Wan Chai, Hung Shing Temple is one of the district's oldest surviving temples, estimated to have been built between 1847 and 1852. Dedicated to Hung Shing, the "God of the South Sea", the temple has long served as an important venue for religious ceremonies and ritual practices, including the housing of soul tablets during its early years, thereby establishing close ties with the Wan Chai community. 

     Exemplifying traditional Lingnan vernacular architecture and seamlessly integrating with the nearby natural rocky terrain, Hung Sing Temple holds immense architectural value. It retains a high degree of authenticity, with well-preserved historic fabric and decorative features, including stone carvings, plaster mouldings, granite figures, and Shiwan ceramic ridge decorations produced in 1909, showcasing both refined craftsmanship and the continuity of traditional building practices. As a significant historic landmark in a modern city, the temple not only reflects Wan Chai's development over the past century, but also stands as a precious reminder of the district's early religious landscape and enduring communal traditions.

     Stanley Mosque, located within Stanley Prison, was constructed between 1936 and 1937. It is the second oldest mosque in Hong Kong and the only mosque situated inside a prison compound. The mosque was initiated, funded, and built by the Indian and Pakistani Muslim staff of the Prisons Department (the predecessor of the Correctional Services Department) together with the local Indian community. 

     Modelled on the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, Pakistan, Stanley Mosque represents a rare building typology in Hong Kong. It is built on a symmetrical plan along an east-west axis oriented toward the Holy Kaaba in Makkah, featuring a flat concrete roof edged by a crenellated parapet and an arcaded facade with horseshoe and ogee ornamental arches. Instead of a typical minaret, Stanley Mosque features minaret-like columns as decoration, maintaining a rich Islamic architectural character. It retains much of its original form, with only minimal alterations made to meet daily operational needs. The mosque not only stands as a testament to the growth of the Muslim community in Hong Kong, but also demonstrates ethnic harmony within society.

     Detailed information on the two monuments is available on the website of the Antiquities and Monuments Office (www.amo.gov.hk/en/historic-buildings/monuments/index.html).

item.title: Hong Kong Customs detects three drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at airport (with photos)
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs on September 29 and yesterday (September 30) detected three drug trafficking cases involving incoming air passengers at Hong Kong International Airport, and seized a total of about 46 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds and a batch of products containing suspected Part I poisons, with a total estimated market value of about $9.2 million. Two men and three women were arrested.

     In the first case, a 32-year-old Filipino male passenger and two Filipino female passengers, aged 24 and 31, arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, on September 29.  During customs clearance, Customs officer found a total of about 35kg of suspected cannabis buds inside their check-in suitcases, and a batch of products containing suspected Part I poisons inside the baggage of the two female passengers. They were then arrested.

     In the second case, a 40-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, via Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, yesterday. During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 6kg of suspected cannabis buds inside his check-in suitcases. He was subsequently arrested.

     In the third case, a 47-year-old Mainland female passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, via Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, yesterday. During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 5kg of suspected cannabis buds inside her check-in suitcases. She was subsequently arrested.

     Investigations of the three cases are ongoing.

     Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not to participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people.

     Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities.

     Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment.

     Under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance, any person who possesses any poison included in Part 1 of the Poisons List other than in accordance with provisions commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $100,000 and imprisonment for two years.

     Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: LD reminds employers and employees to take heat stroke preventive measures in times of Heat Stress at Work Warning
item.description:
​As the Heat Stress at Work Warning is now in effect, the Labour Department (LD) reminds employers and employees to take appropriate measures during the effective period of the warning to prevent heat stroke when working in hot weather or hot environments.
      
     Employees who work outdoors or in non-air-conditioned indoor environments face high levels of heat stress and are at a relatively higher risk of heat stroke. Employers should assess the risk factors of heat stress for employees at work and, based on the identified risk factors, take necessary preventive and control measures, including rescheduling work periods, setting up shading covers, providing ventilation and heat dissipation equipment, and reminding employees to replenish water and rest in a timely manner.
      
     The Heat Stress at Work Warning is formulated by the LD based on the Hong Kong Heat Index, measured temperatures generally over Hong Kong, and the "Extremely Hot Weather" Special Alert. There are three levels of the warning: Amber, Red and Black, which help employers and employees better understand the level of heat stress while working outdoors or indoors without air-conditioning systems.
      
     A spokesman for the LD said that when the department issues the Heat Stress at Work Warning, employers must refer to the criteria and recommendations provided in the "Guidance Notes on Prevention of Heat Stroke at Work" to conduct risk assessments, according to the workloads and other relevant heat stress risk factors, for employees who work outdoors or in non-air-conditioned indoor workplaces. Appropriate rest breaks should be arranged every hour, as far as reasonably practicable, based on various levels of the Heat Stress at Work Warning, to reduce employees' risk of heat stroke.
      
     Employees must also follow instructions to rest on time. Whenever there are any symptoms of heat-related illnesses, such as headache, dizziness, thirst, and nausea, they should rest in a cool and shady place, drink water, and inform employers/supervisors to take appropriate action immediately.
      
     The LD issued the "Guidance Notes on Prevention of Heat Stroke at Work", detailing the various risk factors that should be considered when conducting heat stress risk assessments and recommending corresponding control measures for identified risk factors for employers' and employees' reference. For the Heat Stress at Work Warning and related guidelines, please refer to the department's thematic webpage: www.labour.gov.hk/eng/news/prevention_of_heat_stroke_at_work.htm.

item.title: CE's speech at National Day reception (with photos/video)
item.description:
Following is the speech (English translation) by the Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, at the National Day Reception in Celebration of the 77th Anniversary of the Founding of the People's Republic of China today (October 1):

Distinguished guests, fellow citizens,

     Today marks the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. It carries the special significance of being the first National Day celebrated since the announcement of Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan. 

     Over the past 77 years, the Chinese nation has achieved a historic transformation – from standing up and growing prosperous to becoming strong. Today, China has become the world's largest manufacturer and merchandise trader, its leading contributor to scientific research output and much more, exerting significant influence on international affairs.

     The formulation of a Five-Year Plan for Hong Kong is not merely about rolling out a series of policy initiatives. The Plan provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong, allowing us to apply our unique advantages under "one country, two systems", embrace modern trends and seize the opportunities brought by national development.

     Why should we formulate a Five-Year Plan? And why do it now? The answer is straightforward: to fully and swiftly seize the immense opportunities brought by national development, and to deliver more fruits of development to the benefit of our citizens. Faced with an ever-changing geopolitical landscape, the reshaping of industrial chains, as well as the rapid development of technology and artificial intelligence, Hong Kong must devise a strategic roadmap in a proactive manner and put in place forward-looking plans. As the world's second-largest economy, China is widely recognised as both a driver and a stabiliser for global economic development. Time and tide wait for no man. We must act decisively and respond to changing circumstances by formulating the Five-Year Plan, in order to ride the wave of opportunities, keep pace with the times, and integrate into and serve the overall national development. This can only boost Hong Kong's progress and allow the people of Hong Kong to enjoy more development dividends.

     Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan is a logical and target-oriented plan. It is based on an overall review of Hong Kong's prevailing strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats, and it serves as a comprehensive blueprint targeted at building strengths, overcoming weaknesses, seizing opportunities and managing threats. The Plan focuses on six themes: first, to strengthen the development of "four centres and one hub", namely our status as international financial, maritime and trade centres and an international aviation hub, as well as our development into an international innovation and technology centre and an international hub for high-calibre talent; second, to leverage our advantage as an international city by deepening Hong Kong's development of a legal and dispute resolution services centre, intellectual property trading centre and East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchange; third, to expedite the development of the Northern Metropolis; fourth, to reinforce our strength in connecting with the country and the world; fifth, to enhance social well-being; and sixth, to adopt a holistic approach to development and security. These six themes cover economic development, spatial layout, internal and external connectivity, livelihood enhancement, and risk prevention and control, forming a comprehensive system with interconnected and mutually reinforcing components.

     The three key distinctive features of Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan are: first, it is well-suited to the unique characteristics of Hong Kong. In the Foreword on page 1 of the Plan, it is made clear from the outset that Hong Kong's Five-Year Plan has to be grounded in the city's practical reality, and supported by policy measures and major projects that feature Hong Kong's unique character.

     Second, it adheres to the "one country, two systems" principle. This means that the First Five-Year Plan must be developed under the Basic Law framework. The Basic Law expressly provides for the practice of capitalism and the common law system, as well as the free flow of capital, people, goods and information in Hong Kong, while the First Five-Year Plan stresses a market economy and upholds the two-pronged approach of "effective market" and "capable government".

     Third, the First Five-Year Plan clearly defines Hong Kong's international positioning. Its International Financial Centre chapter points out that we must firmly demonstrate Hong Kong's international positioning, whereas the Policy Address states that we will "stay committed to our global positioning". The two documents reiterate the importance and establishment of Hong Kong's global positioning, which powerfully illustrates that it is part of our city's DNA.

     One of the initiatives for implementing the First Five-Year Plan is to fully leverage Hong Kong's unique advantage as a connector between the country and the rest of the world. Hong Kong is the only city in the world that enjoys the convergence of national and international opportunities. The ultimate focus of the Plan is, in fact, to capitalise on this aggregate advantage: drawing on the momentum of the country's development to gain stable support, while leveraging an international platform to access global resources and achieve two-way interaction. Committed to firmly maintaining its strategic position as the nexus of domestic-international dual circulation, Hong Kong will make greater contributions in its roles as a "super connector" and "super value-adder".

     As the Chinese saying goes, "Victory is ensured when people pool their strength; success is secured when people put their heads together." Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan is the fruit of the collective wisdom gained during our extensive consultation. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government puts words into action. With a strategic vision for a bright new era that drives reform, boosts development, unleashes opportunities and enhances livelihood, we have formulated the 2026 Policy Address to launch wide-ranging policy measures and take forward the initiatives for the first year in line with our five-year strategic blueprint. I am confident that as long as we, each dedicated to our respective roles, join hands and work in synergy with one another, Hong Kong will certainly be able to set out on a path to a brighter and more prosperous future.

     Finally, I wish our motherland and Hong Kong continuing prosperity and stability. May all of you enjoy good health and great success in every endeavour. Thank you very much.

item.title: DH reminds public to take precautions against heat-related illnesses during very hot weather
item.description:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (October 1) reminded members of the public to take appropriate precautions against heat-related illnesses, such as heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, during very hot weather.

     In a high-temperature environment, excessive sweating and difficulty in heat dissipation can cause stress to the body. Members of the public should take the following precautions:
 
  • Hydrate in a timely manner to prevent dehydration;
  • Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting and breathable clothing to minimise heat absorption and facilitate perspiration and heat dissipation;
  • Keep indoor areas well ventilated and maintain appropriate temperature and humidity, e.g. by opening windows or using a fan or air-conditioning;
  • Avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged activities such as hiking or trekking;
  • Arrange outdoor activities in the morning or the late afternoon, if possible, and bring enough water; and
  • Avoid beverages containing caffeine, such as coffee and tea, as well as alcoholic beverages, which may speed up water loss through the urinary system.

     ​In addition, infants and children, the elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease or high blood pressure, overweight people and outdoor/manual workers are more susceptible to heat stroke. These groups should pay special attention to the following:
 
  • Infants and young children: Avoid going outside when the temperature is high. If they must go outside, adults should ensure they stay in places with moderate temperatures and good ventilation or air-conditioning. Infants and young children should never be left unattended in a confined space such as a vehicle;
  • The elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses and overweight people: Pay close attention to health conditions and seek help as soon as possible if experiencing any abnormalities in health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, etc or if there are fluctuations in health conditions. Avoid going out when the temperature is high. Make sure there is good ventilation, or turn on a fan or air-conditioner to keep an appropriate temperature indoors. High temperatures can also worsen the condition of people with chronic illnesses (such as cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). Therefore, they should have an ample supply of their usual medication and keep in contact with family members, neighbours and the community. People should seek immediate help if they feel unwell.
  • Outdoor/manual workers: Reschedule work to cooler hours as far as feasible. If working in a hot environment is unavoidable, provide shade where practicable and use ventilation and heat dissipation equipment. Once work has begun, gradually adjust the pace of work and take breaks in the shade to regain strength.

     ​The DH reminded the public that heat stroke is one of the most common health risks in hot weather. Over the past five years, there have been over 200 hospital admissions due to heat stroke each year in Hong Kong, with two to five fatal cases occurring mainly during the summer months from May to September. Vulnerable groups are more susceptible to heat stroke. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion. In severe cases, patients may suffer from convulsions or become unconscious, which can be life-threatening if they are not cooled down and resuscitated in a timely manner.

     Members of the public are also advised to pay attention to the latest weather, as well as the real-time and forecasted ultraviolet (UV) index released by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). When the UV index is high (6 or above), the public should note the following:
 
  • Avoid direct sunlight exposure to the skin and the eyes;
  • Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen liberally, with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 30 or higher, when participating in outdoor activities. Reapply every two hours if staying outdoors for long periods, or after swimming, sweating or towelling off;
  • While using DEET-containing insect repellents for personal protection against mosquito-borne diseases, apply sunscreen before insect repellent;
  • Seek shade;
  • Wear UV-blocking sunglasses;
  • Wear loose-fitting clothing with long-sleeves; and
  • Wear a wide-brimmed hat or use an umbrella.
    
     ​If symptoms develop, such as dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion, rest and seek help immediately, and seek medical advice as soon as possible.
     
     ​For more health information, the public may visit the CHP's heat stroke page and UV radiation page; the HKO's Dial-a-Weather (1878 200), latest weather report and forecast, UV Index and weather information for hiking and mountaineering; and press releases of the Labour Department on precautions against heat stroke for outdoor workers and their employers when the Heat Stress at Work Warning is in force.

item.title: Police National Security Department conducts arrest operation
item.description:
Police noticed that on the evening of August 31, some people were standing outside MTR Prince Edward Station holding bouquets and shouting seditious slogans. The persons concerned were suspected of spreading false information and attacking the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government with lies, as well as smearing the Police Force, with the intention of inciting hatred against the HKSAR Government and law enforcement agencies.

     The National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force (NSD) attaches great importance to the incident, and swiftly took enforcement actions in Hong Kong Island and Kowloon on September 3 and arrested two local men and one local woman, aged between 33 and 79, for the offence of "doing an act that has a seditious intention with a seditious intention" under Section 24 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance. The three arrestees have been released on bail pending further investigations.

     After follow-up investigations, the NSD took further enforcement actions in Kowloon and the New Territories on September 27 and 28, and arrested a local man and two local women, aged between 46 and 65, for the same offence. The three arrested persons have been released on bail pending further investigations.

     The NSD yesterday (September 30) further arrested a 37-year-old local man and a 58-year-old local woman for the same offence in Kowloon and the New Territories. Prior to the operation, Police obtained court search warrants to search the residences of the arrested persons and seize relevant exhibits. The two arrestees are being detained for further enquiries, while the Police arrest operation is still ongoing.

     Police stressed that the so-called "831 incident" has been proven without factual basis. It is a lie manipulated by persons with ulterior motives to spread lies, attack the HKSAR Government and smear the Police Force, attempting to achieve their political objectives by endangering public peace. The acts concerned are suspected of breaching "doing an act that has a seditious intention with a seditious intention", which is a serious crime. Offenders shall be liable to imprisonment for seven years on first conviction. 

     Police will continue to ensure that laws are observed and strictly enforced to bring offenders to account, so as to prevent, suppress and impose punishment for acts and activities endangering national security.

item.title: FEHD launches two-week "Operation Skynet" to target pest and hygiene issues at food premises
item.description:
​The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) attaches great importance to recent incidents involving pest and rodent infestation and food hygiene in food premises. Apart from following up promptly on individual cases, the department has launched a two-week special inspection and enforcement operation codenamed "Operation Skynet" from today (September 30), targeting supermarkets, restaurants and other premises engaged in the sale, storage or processing of food. The operation will enhance inspections of environmental hygiene, pest and rodent prevention measures, food storage and handling, and whether contaminated food continues to be offered for sale.

     The department will flexibly deploy its operation strategies in response to recent complaints, cases identified through social media and district-level risks. If hygiene or pest and rodent problems are identified, the department will require the premises to make immediate improvements, issue statutory Notices of Elimination of Vermin, and take enforcement action as appropriate. If there is sufficient evidence of a contravention, the FEHD will follow up seriously and institute prosecution in accordance with the law. The FEHD will focus on actual risks, whether immediate improvements have been made, and whether the problems continue to be addressed, rather than measuring its work solely by the number of inspections conducted. If irregularities are found, the department will increase the frequency of inspections and follow-up inspections to ensure that the problems are rectified.

     As of 6pm today, the department inspected 288 supermarkets, 16 restaurants and 23 other food premises, issued 28 Notices of Elimination of Vermin, 22 Notices of Requirement to Cleanse and Repair Food Premises and one warning, and instituted two prosecutions. The department will continue the operation in the next two weeks and adjust its deployment based on the inspection results.

     Regarding the incident at a supermarket on Tong Mei Road in Prince Edward where a rodent was alleged to have crawled over and nibbled on fruits, the FEHD deployed staff to conduct an inspection today, focusing on the rodent infestation, rodent prevention measures and food handling. During the inspection, the hygiene condition of the premises was found to be unsatisfactory. A statutory notice was issued to the person responsible, requiring necessary measures to be taken to eliminate the rodent infestation and carry out cleaning and disinfection. Any food that has been or is reasonably suspected to have been contaminated by rodents must not continue to be offered for sale. The department will follow up on the handling of the food concerned and take action in accordance with the law based on the results of the investigation and evidence collection.

     As for the incident involving a suspected cockroach found in a bowl of noodles at a restaurant in Tai Wai, the department deployed staff to inspect the premises today, focusing on environmental hygiene, food handling procedures and pest and rodent control measures. During the inspection, the FEHD found that the refrigerator door in the food room was damaged and unclean, and instituted prosecution against the person responsible under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X). The FEHD officers also provided the person responsible with food safety and environmental hygiene education, as well as advice on pest and rodent control, reminding them to maintain good food, personal and environmental hygiene at all times and adopt effective pest and rodent control measures. The department will examine the site inspection findings, complaint information and other available objective evidence to clarify the course of events and follow up in accordance with the law.

     The department has also recently been collaborating with the Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health to follow up on two epidemiologically linked cases of human infection with rat Hepatitis E virus. According to the CHP's current epidemiological investigation, the source of infection for the patients is most likely a restaurant they frequently patronised, and it cannot be ruled out that the patients might have come into indirect contact with places or food contaminated by rats or their excreta during the incubation period. The restaurant concerned has suspended operations in accordance with the FEHD's instructions to carry out thorough cleaning, disinfection and rodent control work.

     The FEHD further expanded the scope of its follow-up action today, inspecting not only the restaurant involved but also the shopping mall where it is located, and contacting other tenants to review environmental hygiene and rodent control measures. During the inspections, environmental hygiene and potential pest and rodent infestation problems were identified at certain premises or locations within the shopping mall. A total of seven Notices of Elimination of Vermin were issued to the persons responsible for the premises, requiring improvement measures to be taken. The department will conduct follow-up inspections to ensure that the relevant measures are properly implemented.

     The FEHD has always adopted a risk-based inspection and enforcement strategy. Existing food hygiene and pest and rodent control requirements cover aspects such as environmental hygiene of premises, food storage and handling, prevention of contamination, and pest and rodent control. Food business operators have a responsibility to maintain sound day-to-day hygiene management continuously, detect and address signs of pest and rodent infestation at an early stage, and ensure that contaminated or suspected contaminated food is no longer supplied. Government inspections and enforcement cannot replace operators' responsibility for day-to-day management.

     "Operation Skynet" will also focus on reviewing whether premises have genuinely implemented prevention and control at source, including the handling of refuse and food waste, food storage, rodent prevention facilities, hygiene in back-of-house and storage areas, and environmental factors that may facilitate the entry and exit of rodents or pests. The department will put forward specific improvement requirements to operators based on inspection results and conduct follow-up inspections of key or problematic premises to ensure that improvement measures are not one-off measures but are implemented continuously.

     Rodent control requires corresponding measures to be taken according to the management responsibility for different types of premises. The FEHD is mainly responsible for rodent prevention and eradication in public places within its areas of responsibility, while other government departments are responsible for rodent prevention and eradication at the premises they manage. As for private shopping malls, residential premises and other private premises, day-to-day environmental hygiene and rodent-control work is primarily the responsibility of owners, persons responsible for the premises and property management companies. The FEHD will provide professional advice in response to complaints and specific risk situations, and take action in accordance with the law where necessary.

     To encourage private premises to participate proactively in rodent control, the FEHD has extended the Anti-Rodent Charter to shopping malls, encouraging owners, operators and property management companies to build regular rodent-prevention mechanism. As of September this year, about 130 shopping mall organisations and groups had joined the Charter, covering about 8 200 shops.

     Rodent control is a shared responsibility of the entire community and cannot rely solely on government inspections and rodent eradication work. The Government will continue to monitor, provide support and take action in accordance with the law; the trade, property management companies and persons responsible for various premises must properly carry out day-to-day management; and members of the public must also work together to safeguard environmental hygiene. Only when all parties fulfil their respective responsibilities and start with day-to-day management can an effective and long-term rodent-prevention mechanism be established. Practical rodent prevention and control measures address the three basic elements of rodent survival - food, harbourage and access routes - by cutting off food sources, eliminating hiding places and blocking access routes.

item.title: DH and Police raid premises suspected of illegally supplying and/or possessing unregistered pharmaceutical products for injection treatments (with photos)
item.description:
In view of the fact that certain premises were suspected to provide injectable treatments involving unregistered pharmaceutical products to the public, the Department of Health (DH) conducted a raid in Tsim Sha Tsui today (September 30) in collaboration with the Police. So far, more than 5 900 vials/ampoules of suspected unregistered pharmaceutical products and/or Part 1 poisons have been seized. The case remains under investigation and arrests cannot be ruled out.

     During the operation, the DH and the Police seized more than 5 900 vials/ampoules of suspected unregistered pharmaceutical products and/or Part 1 poisons from two premises in Tsim Sha Tsui, including a company claiming to provide medical health management services.

     Under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance (Cap. 138), any product that meets the definition of a pharmaceutical product must meet the criteria of safety, efficacy and quality, and must be registered with the Pharmacy and Poisons Board of Hong Kong before it may be distributed in Hong Kong. The illegal supply or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products or Part 1 poisons is a criminal offence. Upon conviction, each offence carries a maximum penalty of a fine of $100,000 and imprisonment for two years.

     Where the DH suspects that a person has illegally supplied and/or possessed unregistered pharmaceutical products, it will conduct an investigation and take enforcement action. Where healthcare professionals are involved, the case will be referred to the relevant professional regulatory body for follow-up.

     The DH has been taking stringent enforcement action against the illegal supply and/or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products to safeguard public safety. From 2021 to June 2026, the DH's Drug Office handled 138 cases resulting in convictions for the sale and/or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products. The maximum penalty was 10 months' imprisonment (total for all counts of offences) or a fine of up to $242,000 (the total fine for all counts of offences).

     The DH will continue to closely monitor pharmaceutical products on the market, whether via online or offline channels, in accordance with established mechanisms. The DH will also take appropriate follow-up action upon receiving intelligence or complaints. When necessary, the DH will conduct joint operations with other law enforcement departments, or refer the cases to the relevant department for follow-up.

     Furthermore, the DH has sent a letter to all doctors and private healthcare facilities in Hong Kong, reminding them that they must comply with the law in Hong Kong, as the illegal sale or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products is a criminal offence in Hong Kong.

     The DH also reminded members of the public that injection procedures are medical procedures which should only be performed by locally registered medical practitioners or registered dentists. For queries about disease prevention and treatment, one should first consult a registered doctor, who will provide professional advice based on individual health condition and the latest medical evidence. To protect one's health and safety, do not blindly trust unproven medical claims.

item.title: FEHD continues to combat unlicensed hawking at foreign domestic helpers' gathering places and steps up removal of articles stored in public places (with photos)

A spokesman for the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) said today (September 30) that, to further enhance food safety and environmental hygiene, the department carried out publicity and education work continuously at places where foreign domestic helpers gather across various districts, and stepped up intelligence-led blitz enforcement actions targeting irregularities such as unlicensed hawking, obstruction of passageways, leaving behind or storing articles in public places.

     In the operations conducted over the past three weeks, FEHD officers arrested a total of 10 persons at foreign domestic helpers' gathering places for suspected unlicensed hawking and causing obstruction in public places. About two tonnes of goods, including cooked food, clothes, hats, shoes, handbags and cosmetics, were seized. For the arrested persons suspected of breaching their conditions of stay, the FEHD has notified the relevant law enforcement departments to follow up on the cases in parallel.

     Following the end of the publicity and education period, the FEHD has stepped up patrols and cleaning operations at foreign domestic helpers' gathering places, issuing over 30 notices regarding articles in respect of unattended items, and removing more than 80 kilograms of articles obstructing scavenging work. In addition, regarding setting up of tents in public places and leaving personal belongings behind occupying government land, the department has referred relevant cases to the departments concerned for follow-up.

     The FEHD stressed that foreign domestic helpers engaging in illegal hawking are in breach of their conditions of stay. Employers are urged to remind their domestic helpers to comply with the law and maintain environmental hygiene. The FEHD will continue to conduct proactive inspections at places where foreign domestic helpers commonly gather, step up and further strengthen cross-departmental co-ordination. The FEHD appeals to relevant parties for their full co-operation in maintaining public hygiene. Members of the public may report suspected unlicensed hawking or other irregularities to the FEHD.

item.title: CFS finds Salmonella in Hainanese chicken rice sample
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (September 30) that a sample of Hainanese chicken rice was found to contain a pathogen, Salmonella. The CFS is following up on the incident.

     "The CFS collected the above-mentioned sample from a restaurant in Wan Chai for testing. The test result showed the presence of Salmonella in 25 grams of the sample, exceeding the criterion of the Microbiological Guidelines for Food, which states that Salmonella should not be detected in 25g of a ready-to-eat food sample," a spokesman for the CFS said.

     The CFS has instantly deployed staff to the restaurant concerned for investigation, and has informed the restaurant concerned of the irregularity. The restaurant concerned has already stopped selling and discarded the affected product according to the CFS's instruction. The CFS has provided health education on food safety and hygiene to the person-in-charge and staff of the restaurant, and requested it to improve the food preparation process as well as carrying out thorough cleaning and disinfection according to the CFS's advice.

     According to section 54 of the Public Health and Municipal Services Ordinance (Cap. 132), all food available for sale in Hong Kong, locally produced or imported, should be fit for human consumption. An offender is subject to a maximum fine of $50,000 and imprisonment for six months upon conviction.

     "Salmonella infection may cause fever and gastrointestinal upset such as vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhoea. The effects on infants, young children, the elderly and people with a weak immune system could be more severe and may even lead to death," the spokesman said.

     The CFS will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action to safeguard food safety and public health. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Hong Kong cinema showcased at Odyssey 2026 Film Festival in UK (with photos)

Miss Chau said Hong Kong has long been a meeting point between East and West, between different cultures, languages and creative traditions. item.title: CHP investigates case of human infection of rat Hepatitis E virus epidemiologically linked to previously reported case
item.description:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (September 30) is investigating a case of human infection of rat Hepatitis E virus (HEV). The patient is a family member of another case announced last week and the two cases are epidemiologically linked. The CHP once again urges the public to maintain good personal, food and environmental hygiene, and to implement effective rodent prevention and control measures to prevent rat HEV infection.

Case details
----------------

     Last week, the CHP recorded a rat HEV case involving a 91-year-old man with underlying illnesses. Since then, the CHP and the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) have been investigating the source and route of the infection. One of the male patient's family members, an 80-year-old female, lives in the same Residential Care Home for the Elderly (RCHE) in Kowloon City District. Since the two also share a similar exposure history, the CHP prudently arranged for her to undergo a blood test. Upon laboratory testing by the Public Health Laboratory Services Branch under the CHP, her blood sample tested positive for rat HEV.
 
     The female patient has not exhibited any symptoms of rat HEV and her condition remains stable all along. The CHP will arrange her to undergo further examination and assessment at a hospital.
     
     According to the information provided by the patient, the RCHE staff and the patient's family, the patient had no travel history during the incubation period and no direct contact with rodents, and no rats were observed in the RCHE. Apart from the meals provided by the RCHE, the patient dines at a restaurant in Homantin Plaza with her family at least once or twice a week. Family members of both patients, as well as other residents and staff of the RCHE, are currently asymptomatic and have been put under medical surveillance. No other confirmed cases have been identified so far. Based on the current epidemiological investigation, the CHP believes that it is more likely that patients were infected at the restaurant in question. The CHP does not rule out the possibility that the two patients came into indirect contact with places or food contaminated by rats or their excreta during the incubation period.
 
     Followed an inspection last week, the FEHD conducted another inspection today at the restaurant the patients frequently visited. During the inspection, the FEHD found that the restaurant was still carrying out cleaning and disinfection, and provided staff of the restaurant with environmental hygiene education and advice on pest control. In accordance with the FEHD's instruction, the restaurant suspended operations for thorough cleaning and disinfection, and rodent control work. The FEHD will continue to strengthen cleaning, disinfection and rodent control efforts in the public areas near the locations which the patients visited.

     The CHP and the FEHD will also continue to investigate the source and route of infection of this case.
      
     This is the fourth case of human infection of rat HEV recorded so far this year.
 
Symptoms of rat hepatitis E
-----------------------------------

     Human cases of rat hepatitis E virus infection affect mostly immunocompromised persons. Most cases are asymptomatic, while symptomatic patients reported mild symptoms, such as fatigue, abdominal pain and loss in appetite. It is less likely for patients with rat HEV infection to develop jaundice compared to HEV infected patients.

Prevention
--------------

     The possible routes of transmission of rat HEV to humans include ingestion of food or water contaminated by rodents or their excreta, exposure to environments or objects contaminated by rodents or their excreta and direct contact with rodents or their excreta. The HEV that usually causes human infection is mainly transmitted through the faecal-oral route.

     To prevent infection, the members of the public should maintain good personal, food and environmental hygiene. For example, they should wash their hands thoroughly before eating, store food properly or in the refrigerator, avoid leaving food at room temperature for a long time, and use 1:99 diluted household bleach for general household cleaning and disinfection as household detergents may not kill HEV.

     The Five Keys to Food Safety should be adopted when handling food, i.e. Choose (choose safe raw materials), Clean (keep hands and utensils clean), Separate (separate raw and cooked food), Cook (cook thoroughly) and Safe Temperature (keep food at a safe temperature), to prevent food-borne diseases.

     In general, rodents (such as rats) can transmit multiple diseases to humans, both directly and indirectly. The public is advised to take the following measures:
 
  • Eliminate sources of food and nesting places for rodents in the living environments. Store food in covered containers and handle pet food properly to prevent it from becoming food for rodents;
  • Store all refuse and food remnants in dustbins with well-fitted covers. Dustbins must be emptied at least once a day;
  • Keep premises, especially refuse rooms and stairways, clean. Avoid accumulation of articles;
  • Inspect all flower beds and pavements regularly for signs of rodent infestation; and
  • Avoid the high-risk activities below to reduce rodent contact:
     - Avoid contact with rodents and areas contaminated by rodent excreta;
     - Avoid handling rodents with bare hands;
     - Wash hands with liquid soap and water immediately after handling animals, and disinfect contaminated areas; and
     - If a wound appears, clean the broken skin immediately and cover it properly with waterproof adhesive dressings.

     Rodent control requires co-operation from all sectors of society. The CHP urged the public to strengthen rodent prevention and control measures and co-operate with government's efforts to reduce the risk of rat HEV transmission.

item.title: CFS follows up on aquatic product imported from Japan suspected of breaching Food Safety Order
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (September 30) that an aquatic product from a regulated Japanese prefecture was suspected to be in breach of the relevant Food Safety Order when the CFS inspected food imported from Japan. The product concerned has been marked and sealed by the CFS and has not entered the market. The CFS is following up on the case.

     A spokesman for the CFS said, "During an inspection of a consignment of food imported from Japan, the CFS found a carton of dried barracuda product sourced from Chiba Prefecture after the Order was issued. The importer concerned is thus suspected of breaching the relevant Order."

     According to the Order, all aquatic products originating from 10 metropolises/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, are prohibited from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong if they are harvested, manufactured, processed or packed on or after August 24, 2023, including all live, chilled, frozen, dried or otherwise preserved aquatic products, sea salt, and unprocessed or processed seaweed.

     The CFS will continue to follow up on this incident and take appropriate action, including informing the Japanese authorities concerned of the incident. Prosecution will be instituted against the importer concerned should there be sufficient evidence. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Incoming passenger convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and alternative smoking products (with photo)
item.description:
​An incoming female passenger was sentenced to six months' imprisonment and fined $2,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (September 30) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes, failing to declare them to Customs officers, as well as importing alternative smoking products, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO) and the Import and Export Ordinance (IEO).
      
     Customs officers intercepted a 50-year-old incoming Mainland female passenger arriving in Hong Kong from Tokyo, Japan, at Hong Kong International Airport yesterday (September 29) and seized about 2 400 duty-not-paid cigarettes and 32 000 alternative smoking products, with an estimated market value of about $107,000 and a duty potential of about $8,000, from her personal baggage. The passenger was subsequently arrested.
      
     Customs welcomes the sentence. The custodial sentence has imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflects the seriousness of the offences.
      
     Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, tobacco products are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys duty-not-paid tobacco commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.
      
     Under the IEO, any person who imports an alternative smoking product into Hong Kong commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.
      
     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: French Science Festival "Food (R)Evolutions" exhibition at Hong Kong Science Museum to showcase the science behind cooking (with photos)
item.description:
The Hong Kong Science Museum (HKScM) is collaborating with the Consulate General of France in Hong Kong and Macau to launch the "Food (R)Evolutions" exhibition from October 1 to October 28 at the Exhibition Hall on the ground floor of the HKScM. Bringing together culture, science and innovation, the exhibition showcases the science behind cooking. The exhibition is a programme of the French Science Festival.
      
     Addressing the opening ceremony today (September 30), the Acting Deputy Director of Leisure and Cultural Services (Culture), Mr Ng Chi-wo, expressed gratitude to the Consulate General of France in Hong Kong and Macau for bringing to visitors the fascinating exhibition and an exciting array of extension activities. The exhibition also showcases iconic Hong Kong delicacies whose making techniques are inscribed onto the Intangible Cultural Heritage Inventory of Hong Kong. Combining French scientific insights with Hong Kong's popularly beloved craftsmanship, the exhibition allows visitors to fully appreciate the scientific depth underpinning both food cultures.
      
     Other officiating guests included the Deputy Consul General of France in Hong Kong and Macau, Mr Benjamin Hubin, and the Museum Director of the HKScM, Mr Patrick Lau.
      
     The exhibition will introduce scientists from different eras dedicated to studying ingredients and their transformations, and will explore molecular gastronomy techniques, future dietary trends, sustainable diets, senior-friendly diets, space food and more. A dedicated corner "Taste of Hong Kong" explores the science behind the distinctive textures, aromas and tastes of iconic "cha chaan teng" favourites, including pineapple buns, egg tarts and milk tea. The exhibition will also showcase gerontech innovations designed to support elderly dining provided by the LU Jockey Club Gerontech-X Lab of Lingnan University, along with molecular gastronomy tools provided by the Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
      
     To complement the exhibition, the HKScM will roll out a series of free extension programmes. For details of the exhibition and activities, please visit the website at www.spu.hk/en/cards/french-science-festival-2026/.

item.title: First award ceremony for Packaging Reduction Charter held (with photos)
item.description:
The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) today (September 30) held the first award ceremony for the Packaging Reduction Charter to commend businesses for their outstanding contributions to reducing packaging waste in 2025-26. A total of 75 signatory companies to the Charter were being honoured. Participating companies reduced approximately 13 000 tonnes of packaging materials in total, which is equivalent to the weight of about 900 double-decker buses.
 
     Speaking at the award ceremony, the Under Secretary for Environment and Ecology, Miss Diane Wong, said that this year marks the opening year of the National 15th Five-Year Plan. The plan clearly sets out to accelerate the comprehensive green transition of economic and social development, leveraging carbon peaking and carbon neutrality as drivers to enhance the momentum for green development. To proactively align with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) also mentions that the EPD will deepen the reform of the municipal solid waste management system, striving to move away from reliance on landfill disposal for municipal solid waste directly by 2035, with a view to achieving "Zero Landfill".
 
     She stated that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government has long adopted a practical and feasible approach, actively collaborating with the trades to explore and promote packaging waste reduction in Hong Kong. She commended the awardees for their persistent efforts and contributions, emphasising that the commercial and industrial sectors' active efforts in waste reduction at source are crucial for Hong Kong's progress towards "Zero Landfill" and carbon neutrality. She thanked various sectors for their efforts in environmental protection, and appealed for more companies to join in the future to jointly promote a green business culture.
 
     The five assessment criteria for the Charter are "Packaging Reduction", "Packaging Recyclability", "Packaging Reuse/Recycling", "Sustainable Packaging", and "Promotion of Packaging Reduction". Awardees were presented with Platinum, Gold, and Merit awards respectively. The list of awardees is available on the thematic website of the Charter (www.lesspackaging.hk).
 
     The EPD launched the Charter in March last year to encourage businesses to reassess and reduce their packaging usage, foster a waste reduction culture in commercial activities, and support Hong Kong's long-term goals of "Zero Landfill" and carbon neutrality. So far, a total of 148 local and multinational companies have signed the Charter, covering about 3 000 service and retail outlets across the territory in various retail and catering categories. This reflects that the Charter has been well received by the trades and has delivered remarkable results.
 
     To assist businesses in packaging reduction and management, the EPD has published the Practical Guides on Packaging Reduction and Management (Practical Guides) for eight specific sectors (Note) on its website for the trades' reference. In addition, to address the substantial increase in parcels, cartons, and filling materials arising from the rapid development of online shopping, the EPD has, starting from 2026, collaborated with major logistics companies to progressively implement the Self-pickup Store On-site Recycling Project. This facilitates the on-site return of packaging materials by members of the public for reuse and recycling immediately after collecting their parcels at the self-pickup stores. For the latest information on the Charter, please refer to the thematic website.
 
Note: The eight specific sectors are supermarkets and grocery stores, logistics, e-commerce, hotel and hospitality, electronics and electrical appliances, beverage manufacturing, food manufacturing, and importers.

item.title: Inter-departmental Task Force against Illegal Employment convenes third meeting (with photos)
item.description:
The Secretary for Security, Mr Tang Ping-keung, chaired the third meeting of the Inter-departmental Task Force against Illegal Employment today (September 30). At the meeting, the Task Force discussed measures to combat illegal employment in the 2026 Policy Address, followed up on the latest situation of illegal employment, and agreed to co-opt the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau (CEDB), the Development Bureau (DEVB), the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD), the Home Affairs Department (HAD) and the Tourism Commission (TC) as members of the Task Force, with a view to combating illegal employment in key industries. 

     The Convenor of the Task Force, Mr Tang, said, "The Chief Executive announced in the 2026 Policy Address an array of measures to step up efforts to combat illegal employment on all fronts. In particular, after reviewing the latest trends of illegal employment, the Task Force has designated catering and cleaning, renovation and construction, retail, food delivery, transport and logistics as well as tourism as key industries, and co-opted relevant bureaux and departments as members of the Task Force in order to strengthen the functions of the Task Force and curb illegal employment in these key industries in a targeted manner. In addition, we will invite relevant sectors to nominate representatives as 'Anti-Illegal Employment Ambassadors', who will join hands with the Government in combating illegal employment. They will assist in intelligence collection to widen our intelligence network and step up publicity and education in relevant sectors so as to raise awareness of not employing illegal workers."

     At the same time, under the co-ordination of the Task Force, relevant departments will actively take forward other measures in the 2026 Policy Address, including leveraging technology to enhance the effectiveness of cyber patrol and intelligence collection; reviewing the penalty for illegal employment and striving for sentences with a greater deterrent effect to be handed down by courts; and enhancing interdepartmental joint operations, with a view to stepping up efforts in combating illegal employment on all fronts.  

     Established by the Security Bureau in September 2025, the Task Force aims to enhance interdepartmental co-ordination to combat illegal employment under a multipronged approach. After the addition of new members, members of the Task Force include the CEDB, the DEVB, the Education Bureau, the Labour and Welfare Bureau, the Transport and Logistics Bureau, the FEHD, the HAD, the Hong Kong Police Force, the Immigration Department, the Labour Department, the TC and the Transport Department.

item.title: Hong Kong Customs steps up consumer protection work during Mainland's National Day Golden Week period (with photos)
item.description:
With the Mainland's National Day Golden Week approaching, Hong Kong Customs has stepped up patrols at popular shopping spots in various districts since yesterday (September 29) and reminded traders to comply with the requirements of the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (TDO), with a view to safeguarding the rights of local consumers and visitors.
     
     Apart from patrolling popular shopping spots, Customs officers will also drive publicity at medicine shops, dried seafood and ginseng shops, facial and beauty shops and jewellery shops in different tourist shopping areas such as Yau Tsim Mong, Hung Hom, To Kwa Wan and Causeway Bay. Retail shops and workers in the tourist industry will be reminded to comply with the requirements of the TDO.

      Customs officers will also distribute pamphlets at different land boundary control points to remind visitors and local consumers that they should patronise shops with good reputations. They should have a good understanding of a product's specifications and make comparisons before purchasing. They are also reminded to check carefully the total price and unit price of the goods before making payment, and to retain transaction receipts and related records, which can serve as evidence in case a complaint is lodged in the future. They are additionally reminded to check with the trademark owners or their authorised agents if the authenticity of a product is in doubt.

     Customs is concerned about visitors being misled into making purchases by unfair trade practices, and has established a Quick Response Team to handle urgent complaints lodged by short-term visitors. The complaints will be promptly referred to investigators for priority handling.

     Under the TDO, any trader who adopts unfair trade practices, including making false trade descriptions in relation to goods, misleading omissions, aggressive commercial practices as well as bait and switch practices, or sells or possesses for sale any goods with a forged trademark, commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for five years.
      
     Members of the public may report suspected violations of the TDO to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Joint Working Group on Commodity Trading convenes first meeting (with photos)
item.description:
The Joint Working Group on Commodity Trading (Working Group), led by the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, held its first meeting today (September 30).

At its first meeting today, the Working Group held in-depth discussions on the policy directions and objectives for developing commodities trading, and explored key areas including market trends and Hong Kong's development potential. The Working Group will continue to follow up on various priority projects, with a view to formulating a clear development roadmap to build an internationally competitive commodities trading ecosystem for Hong Kong.

     Mr Hui said, "As the global commodities market landscape undergoes profound evolution, we are taking proactive steps to open up new growth points while consolidating Hong Kong's existing strengths in the financial market. Leveraging Hong Kong's unique advantage of connecting the Mainland and the world under 'one country, two systems', we are taking gold as an entry point to forge ahead with the development of an international commodities trading ecosystem in alignment with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. The Working Group will thoroughly implement the strategic deployments of the Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) to transform Hong Kong into an international commodities hub that integrates trading, clearing, warehousing, pricing and financing, thereby better serving the overall national development."

item.title: Hong Kong Customs arrests company director suspected of supplying baby hair and body wash with false trade descriptions (with photo)
item.description:
​Hong Kong Customs recently arrested a female director of a trading company suspected of supplying baby hair and body wash with false trade descriptions, in contravention of the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (TDO).
      
     Customs earlier received a referral from the Consumer Council alleging that the ingredients of a baby hair and body wash in the market were inconsistent with its product claim. Customs officers swiftly test-purchased the baby hair and body wash concerned from a retailer in Causeway Bay and sent samples to the Government Laboratory for examination. Examination results confirmed that the baby hair and body wash, which was labelled as free of allergenic fragrances, contained the fragrance allergen limonene at a concentration of 0.11%. Limonene possesses a citrus aroma. Limonene, when exposed to air, can oxidise into allergenic products that may trigger skin allergies in some individuals.
      
     Customs subsequently launched a follow-up investigation to inspect retailers selling baby wash across various districts. During the operation, Customs seized a total of 34 bottles of the same baby hair and body wash from eight retail shops. A 42-year-old female director of a trading company was arrested.
      
     An investigation is ongoing and the arrested woman has been released on bail pending further investigation.
      
     Customs reminds traders to comply with the requirements of the TDO and consumers to procure products at reputable shops.
      
     Under the TDO, any person who supplies goods with a false trade description in the course of trade or business, or is in possession of any goods for sale with a false trade description, commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for five years.
      
     Members of the public may report any suspected violations of the TDO to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: CHP investigates imported Mpox case
item.description:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) said today (September 30) that it is investigating an imported Mpox (also known as Monkeypox) case. Due to the significant increase in Mpox cases recently, the CHP strongly urged individuals who have engaged in high-risk sexual contact, particularly with strangers, to remain vigilant and take appropriate personal protective measures, including receiving the Mpox vaccination. Close physical contact with anyone suspected of having contracted Mpox must be avoided. The CHP emphasised that unsafe sexual contact increases the risk of infection.
      
     The CHP has implemented a series of targeted prevention and control measures, including setting up an Mpox hotline (2125 2373) to conduct close contact tracing, provide health assessments and arrange vaccination services, collaborating with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to provide outreach vaccination services; strengthening the promotion of safer sex in high-risk venues (e.g. saunas), and collaborating with operators of relevant dating apps to disseminate prevention messages. The first outreach vaccination service, co-organised by the CHP and one of the NGOs, the Community Health Organisation for Intervention, Care and Empowerment, was successfully held yesterday (September 29). Approximately 50 people received the Mpox vaccination. Due to CHP's multipronged approach, around 120 individuals with high-risk exposure have received the Mpox vaccination over the past week at the facilities operated by the DH or the Hospital Authority (HA) that offer Mpox vaccinations.

Case details
--------------

     The case involves a 40-year-old man who developed rashes on various parts of his body, including his genital area, oral cavity and limbs, on September 20. He developed a fever on September 28 and sought medical attention the following day at a social hygiene service (SocHS) clinic under the DH. He was arranged to receive isolation treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital. Upon laboratory testing by the CHP's Public Health Laboratory Services Branch, his clinical specimen tested positive for the Monkeypox virus. The patient is currently in stable condition.
      
     According to information provided by the patient, he had high-risk sexual exposure outside Hong Kong during the incubation period. The CHP is continuing its epidemiological investigation of the case and will report it to the World Health Organization.

Number of Mpox cases have shown a sustained increase since August
---------------------------------------------------

     Since 2022, Hong Kong has recorded 113 Mpox cases (89 local cases and 24 imported cases), including the above-mentioned case. All patients are males. The number of Mpox cases in Hong Kong has increased since August. As of today, 29 cases have been recorded this year, including 22 local cases and seven imported cases. Among them, 20 were new cases reported since August. Epidemiological investigations showed that of the 20 recently identified cases, all patients reported engaging in high-risk sexual behaviours during the incubation period including having sex with male strangers or multiple partners, and having sex without a condom. A total of 12 patients used dating apps to find casual sexual partners. Most of the patients had not received the Mpox vaccine and around 40 per cent of them are infected with Human Immunodeficiency Virus. The CHP's Public Health Laboratory Services Branch conducted genetic analysis of the virus and found that some cases had identical genetic sequences. This suggests that they may have shared a common source of infection, with several transmission chains existing among men who have sex with men population. Despite conducting in-depth epidemiological investigations, the CHP has been unable to contact some newly met sexual partners of some of the confirmed Mpox cases. This has hindered the CHP's ability to effectively conduct contact tracing and implement corresponding prevention and control measures. Therefore, the CHP strongly urged the public to keep their sexual partners’ contact information to facilitate contact tracing when necessary.

Stepping up public education and outreach efforts
-------------------------------------------------------------

     The CHP urged individuals who have engaged in high-risk sexual contact to seek medical attention immediately if they develop symptoms associated with Mpox, such as a rash, fever or swollen lymph nodes. The CHP has set up an Mpox hotline (2125 2373) to provide health assessments advice and vaccination arrangements for affected individuals. The hotline operates daily from 9am to 6pm.

     In addition, the CHP has stepped up its Mpox prevention and control outreach on social media platforms (including dating apps) and is collaborating with relevant NGOs (including the Community Health Organisation for Intervention, Care and Empowerment; the Hong Kong AIDS Foundation; and the Hong Kong Christian Service) to arrange outreach vaccination services. The CHP also deployed staff to conduct health promotion activities at a number of entertainment venues, including sauna establishments. The CHP has also arranged with the operators of relevant dating apps to send pop-up messages to users in Hong Kong through the app, warning them of the risks of unsafe sexual contact and promoting Mpox vaccination.

Getting vaccinated to prevent Mpox
-----------------------------------------

     The Mpox vaccine can prevent infection and severe disease. The DH provides Mpox vaccination services for high-risk groups, including individuals with high-risk sexual practices (such as having multiple sexual partners), sex workers, or having a history of sexually transmitted infection within the past 12 months. High-risk target groups can receive Mpox walk-in vaccinations at any of the DH's SocHS (namely Chai Wan SocHS, Wan Chai Male SocHS, Wan Chai Female SocHS, Yau Ma Tei Male SocHS, Yau Ma Tei Female SocHS, Yung Fung Shee SocHS, Fanling SocHS and Tuen Mun SocHS) and the DH's Yau Ma Tei Integrated Treatment Centre, without prior appointments. Meanwhile, the DH's Kowloon Bay Integrated Treatment Centre and the HA's Special Medical Clinics at Queen Elizabeth Hospital and Princess Margaret Hospital also provide Mpox vaccination services for their clients.
      
     In response to the significant recent increase in Mpox cases, the DH has established an additional Mpox vaccination centre at the CHP Building at 147C Argyle Street in Mong Kok to administer Mpox vaccinations to high-risk groups. Members of the high-risk target groups may call the aforesaid Mpox hotline to arrange their vaccination with DH staff.
